attack_ability_system:
Player attack and ability companion actor system (Bank 02).

Runs as a companion actor spawned before the movement controller via SpawnBefore. Each frame, checks player state (alive, not in hurt/knockback/dialogue) and listens for the attack button. The COP mask is $0081: bit 0 only tells BranchIfPressed/BranchIfNotPressed to test joypadRaw (the physical level, which still reports a button that was consumed through joypadHeld) instead of joypadCurrent, and $0080 is the logical attack bit, physical A in this ROM (db-us/transforms.json rewrites the vanilla ROM masks of this block; the vanilla attack mask differs). Dispatches to character-specific attack flows based on characterForm ($0AD4): Will (form 0) uses WillAttackDispatch, Freedan (form 1) uses FreedanAttackDispatch. Forms 2+ return immediately and cannot attack through this code path.

Both characters share a 40-frame ($28 hex) initial button-hold detection period via COP LoopInit. If the player releases during this window, the attack cancels back to idle.

Will's attack system (WillAttackDispatch):
- Extended charge timer: 120 frames ($0078)
- Ability gate: abilityBitmask bit 2 ($0004) unlocks Spin Dash
- Without bit 2: release after charge → Psycho Dash
- With bit 2: CheckAttackChargeable gates continued charge; L/R ($0030) → Spin Dash; release → Psycho Dash
- Psycho Dash: directional fast dash with trail afterimage actors (4 directions)
- Spin Dash: spawns a GuidedProjectileActor the player steers with D-pad; the charge level $26 starts at $0F and four alternating L, R, L, R presses (SpinDashChargeTick) bring it below $0C, which ends the charge phase

Freedan's attack system (FreedanAttackDispatch):
- Extended charge timer: 100 frames ($0064)
- Additional cancel: L/R ($0030, tested in joypadCurrent) during the charge aborts to AttackCleanup; the vanilla ROM mask also listed the Y and A face bits, which the transform drops because the attack button is logical $0080 here
- Ability gate: abilityBitmask bit 5 ($0020) unlocks Aura Barrier
- Without bit 5: release → Dark Friar
- With bit 5: D-pad during charge → cancel (AttackChargeReturn); L/R ($0030) → Aura Barrier; release → Dark Friar
- Dark Friar: 4-directional energy projectile with trail, wall-bounce, redirect (upgrade level 2), and fragment burst on hit
- Aura Barrier: requires standing still; rotating orbital projectiles with VRAM DMA, custom palette, expand/shrink lifecycle

Ability bitmask ($0AA2) gates (the bits are event flags $0510 + characterForm×4 + slot, the flags the inventory Status tab tests with TestAbilityFlag):
- Bit 0 ($0001): Psycho Dash (Will attack gate + charge release)
- Bit 1 ($0002): Psycho Slider (Will run attack)
- Bit 2 ($0004): Spin Dash (Will L/R alternate ability)
- Bit 4 ($0010): Dark Friar (Freedan attack gate + charge release)
- Bit 5 ($0020): Aura Barrier (Freedan L/R alternate ability)
- Bit 6 ($0040): Earthquaker (Freedan attack gate)

The system hijacks the player actor function pointer via SetPlayerActorFunc during ability execution, then restores it through AttackCleanup which kills spawned FX actors and plays form-specific palette restoration (Will=#0B, Freedan=#0C).

Helper routines: ValidateAttackReady ($3A00 flags + facing < 4), ValidateAttackContinue ($2B00 per-frame check), CheckAttackChargeable (carry clear only while playerFlags $8000 is clear and the player body animation index at +$28 is 0–3 or $10–$13), SavePlayerPosition (snapshots for offset calculations), ComputeParentOffset/ApplyParentOffset (relative position tracking for child actors), KillSpawnedProjectile (cleanup via MarkDeath).

Palette FX (bundle contents decoded from palette_bundles): WillAttackPaletteFX = #2A twice then #2B forever; FreedanAttackPaletteFX = #4B twice then #2C forever (both tint the 15 colors at CGRAM $81–$8F, which AttackCleanup restores with the single-frame bundles #0B/#0C); AuraBarrierPaletteFX = #5B forever (8 colors at CGRAM $A1–$A8, a blue-to-white ramp, 16 ticks per cycle). Dark Friar also starts bundle #4A through a thinker: a white flash on $81–$8F fading back to Freedan's normal colors over 36 ticks.

Ability tables: LoadAbilityDamageA (will_ability_damage_table, Will) and LoadAbilityDamageB (freedan_ability_damage_table, Freedan) do not hold sprite or hitbox data. Each 6-byte record is { word 0, word pointer to the ability's upgrade-level word, then one damage byte per level }; the loader reads the level from that WRAM word ($0B16 Psycho Dash, $0B18 Psycho Slider, $0B1A Spin Dash; $0B1C Dark Friar, $0B1E Aura Barrier, $0B20 Earthquaker) and stores record[4 + level] to climbStateData ($09E0, Will) or $09E2 (Freedan), the damage bonus that combat_collision adds to the hit strength. Values by level: Psycho Dash 5/10, Psycho Slider 5/8, Spin Dash 4/7; Dark Friar 5/8/12, Aura Barrier 5/9, Earthquaker 0/7.

=== TRAIL FOLLOWERS (TrailFollowerSprA, 179702–179872) ===

Dark Friar fragment trail follower actors and position offset helpers. Provides two trail segment actor variants (TrailFollowerSprA sprite #05, TrailFollowerSprB sprite #06) that follow behind Dark Friar fragment projectiles to create a cascading afterimage effect. Both variants share the same loop logic — only their initial sprite/hitbox configuration differs.

The trail system works via a 3-stage position FIFO buffer stored in per-actor long-address scratch fields ($7F0000–$7F001A,X). Each frame, TrailPositionCascade shifts the parent actor's current position into stage 3 of the queue, while each older position advances one stage forward. The trail actor displays the position from stage 1 (the oldest buffered value), creating a 3-frame position delay. The position source is the actor in $04 (the previous entry of the actor list, i.e. the actor the follower was inserted after, not a stored parent id): TrailFollowerSprA is spawned last, so it sits directly behind the fragment and lags it by 3 frames, while TrailFollowerSprB (spawned first) follows A and therefore lags the fragment by about 6. TrailPositionInit seeds all 3 stages with the current position so the trail starts co-located with its parent.

ComputeParentOffset and ApplyParentOffset are also in this part — they store/apply the XY delta between current position and a parent actor, used by Dark Friar projectile and trail actors for relative positioning.

=== SECTIONS (the block has no parts in blocks.json; the notes use these address ranges) ===

178099–179701: AttackSystemEntry, both dispatch paths, all Freedan abilities (Dark Friar, Aura Barrier) and the shared helpers.
179702–179825: TrailFollowerSprA/B, TrailPositionCascade, TrailPositionInit.
179826–179871: ComputeParentOffset, ApplyParentOffset (they use the spawner slot stored in $24 by CopyActorState).
179872–180391: Psycho Dash and its four trail actors. 180393–180763: Spin Dash, SpinDashChargeTick. 180764–181131: KillSpawnedProjectile, GuidedProjectileActor, the palette FX actors, RecomputeProjectilePos and the two ability-table loaders.

=== CONVENTIONS ===

- Actor flags $10: bit 13 ($2000) = hidden for SortActorsByDepth and the script-only path of RunActors_Normal (no collision-aware movement, no iframe handling); bit 14 ($4000) = off-screen flag maintained by the depth sort; bit 7 ($0080) = hit/iframe marker.
- $12 bits $2000 / $4000 negate the Y / X movement of staged movement chains (so one chain runs south or north, east or west).
- COP movement operands (StageMoveXY, StageSpriteMoveX/Y, StageSpriteLoopMoveX/Y) are indices into move_chain_table, not distances: index 1/3/5/7 = constant +1/+2/+3/+4 per frame, 2/4/6 = the negatives, index $36 = 8 frames of 0, then 4,4,7,7,9,9,12,12, then 0,0, then eight frames of −8.
- LoopStart/LoopEnd yield once per iteration, so LoopStart(#n) is an n-frame loop.

camera_tilemap:
Camera tilemap rendering, VRAM DMA transfer, and scroll stripe management (Bank 02).

Implements the complete pipeline for updating SNES background layer tilemaps in response to camera scrolling. The system manages two BG layers (indexed by X=0 for layer 0, X=2 for layer 1) with independent scroll positions, using four staging buffers from $7E3100 (a column strip and a row strip per layer; initial pointers $06B2/$06B4 = column strips, $06B6/$06B8 = row strips, set by system_init) to prepare tilemap data for DMA transfer during V-Blank.

Naming: RenderColumnStrip, DmaColumnStrip and the $06B2/$06B4 buffers deal with COLUMN strips (a vertical run of 16 metatiles, DMA'd with VRAM increment 32), while RenderRowStrip, DmaRowStrip and the $06B6/$06B8 buffers deal with ROW strips. UpdateScrollRow/UpdateScrollColumn and the Fill*TilemapSeg routines use the geometric meaning, so the two vocabularies meet inside this file.

Two primary modes:
- CameraFullRefresh: Redraws the whole 64-tile-wide tilemap of one layer: wraps the camera target into the map bounds, then renders 32 metatile columns 16px apart via RenderColumnStrip and immediately DMA-transfers each one to VRAM. Called on scene load.
- CameraSmoothScroll: Per-frame incremental scroll. Deltas are clamped to ±16px per frame for smooth motion. When scrolling crosses a 16px tile boundary (detected by XOR of old/new positions on bit 4), the newly-visible row or column is rendered into the staging buffer for DMA during V-Blank.

The rendering pipeline (RenderColumnStrip, RenderRowStrip) converts map tile indices to 2×2 VRAM tilemap entries (16×16 metatiles → four 8×8 tiles), handles nametable wrapping via WrapMapIndex, and writes to the staging buffer. FillHorizTilemapSeg and FillVertTilemapSeg are the inner loops that expand metatile indices into VRAM-format tilemap words.

FlushDirtyTilemapStrips is called during V-Blank (NMI) to DMA any staged horizontal and vertical strips to VRAM using DmaColumnStrip (column strips: two 64-byte tile columns) and DmaRowStrip (row strips: two 128-byte halves, one per nametable).

Bg3TilemapVramDma uploads the BG3 tilemap staging buffer at $7F0200 (bg3TilemapBuffer, used by the console string renderer) to the BG3 tilemap at VRAM $7800 during V-Blank: a full transfer ($0800 bytes = the whole 32×32 map, displayModeFlags bit 0) or a partial one ($0140 bytes = five tile rows starting at row 2, bits 4/5). BG3SC is initialised to $78, which places the BG3 tilemap at $7800.
DisplaySceneTitle:
Scene title display system - centered area name overlay during scene transitions (172315-172521, Bank 02).

Called from ClearSceneState after actor spawning and before thinker spawning and palette loading. Displays the current scene's area name (e.g. 'South Cape', 'Edward's Castle') in a one-row dialogue box, giving the player a visual cue of the new location.

=== DISPLAY PIPELINE (DisplaySceneTitle) ===

1. Scene change guard: compares $0D6E (the scene just left, recorded by ExecuteSceneTransition; for a world-map entry it is the deferred destination) against sceneCurrent ($0644). If they are equal (a reload of the same scene ID) the title is suppressed.

2. Width measurement: CountTitleGlyphs walks the scene title wide-string, counting visible characters while expanding dictionary references ($D6/$D7) and cursor advances ($CC). The string is the one stored right after the scene's actor list: SpawnSceneActors leaves $3E on the list's $FF terminator and CountTitleGlyphs moves it one byte on, to the first title byte. Returns the glyph count in $00.

3. Empty title guard: if the count is zero the routine returns immediately (177 of the 241 scene records have an empty title, only $CA).

4. Centering: (18 - glyphCount), forced even by AND $FE, used as a byte offset into the VRAM write buffer, i.e. (18 - N) / 2 tile cells. 18 is presumably the interior of the 10-column box if a column is 2 tiles wide (inferred; there is no clamp for N > 18).

5. Box setup: sets $00B4 = $E0 (nonzero flag that makes ExecuteSceneTransition wait for a button press) and clears $00B5. Opens the box via scene_title_box_format ([DLG:7,7][SIZ:A,1]), i.e. a DialogStringRenderer OpenDialogueBox command with width $0A and height 1 at position (7, 7).

6. Centered render: adds the padding to the VRAM write cursor ($0998), then calls DialogStringRenderer a second time with the title string pointer.

=== GLYPH COUNTING (CountTitleGlyphs) ===

A specialized wide-string character counter for the commands found in scene title strings:
- Literal tiles (< $C0): 1 glyph each
- $CA (Return): ends the count
- $CC (AdvanceCursor): adds the operand byte to the count
- $D6/$D7 (DictionaryA/B): looks up the word in dialog_dictionary_a/b and counts each expanded character up to its $CA terminator
- Other commands (>= $C0): skips one operand byte without counting

The scan starts at [$3E] + 1. SpawnSceneActors ends with $3E pointing at the $FF that closes the scene's actor list (scene_lifecycle calls DisplaySceneTitle right after it), and the title string follows that terminator directly in the scene record (see scene_actors). INC $3E steps over the $FF; it is not a type or length byte, and the title's first byte is counted.
DmaWordToVram:
DMA word transfer to VRAM — single-routine utility (164770–164795, Bank 02).

Configures DMA channel 0 for a word-size (16-bit) transfer to VRAM register $2118/$2119. Input: X = source address (low 16 bits), A = source bank byte, Y = transfer size in bytes. Sets DMAP0 to mode $01 (word transfer, auto-increment), B-bus target $18 (VDATA), then fires DMA channel 0 via MDMAEN. Caller must set VMADDL ($2116) to the target VRAM address before calling.
event_blocks:
Event block tile system — runtime map edits (doors, bridges, barriers) driven by event flags (172521–173533, Bank 02).

An event block copies a rectangle of map tiles from a source position over a destination position, either instantly (CopyEventBlockTiles) or animated with VRAM updates (AnimateEventBlock). Despite its name CopyEventBlockTiles does not exchange the two rectangles: the source is left unchanged.

=== EVENT FLAG INDEXING ===

ApplyAllEventBlocks walks the 32-byte event flag bitfield at $0A20 (LSR per bit). For every set flag the event index ($04, 8-bit, wraps after 256 indices) goes through LookupEventBlock; when the scene matches, CopyEventBlockTiles runs. Callers: scene_lifecycle and inventory_overlay. Defeated-enemy blocks call LookupEventBlock + CopyEventBlockTiles from actor_execution; COP #32 StageBgChange calls LookupEventBlock and COP #33 ApplyBgChange loops AnimateEventBlock.

=== EVENT BLOCK TABLE FORMAT ===

LookupEventBlock reads 8-byte entries from event_block_table (index × 8) into WRAM $0096-$00A8 (absolute addresses, used as DP with D = 0):
  Byte 0: Scene ID — must match sceneCurrent or the entry is skipped (carry set = no match)
  Bytes 1-2: Source tile X/Y ($96/$98)
  Byte 3: Width ($A2, and $9E as the column counter); byte 4: height ($A0)
  Bytes 5-6: Destination tile X/Y ($9A/$9C)
  Byte 7: Layer flag ($A4) — 0 = layer 0 (mapLayerTilemap + collisionLayer), nonzero = layer 1 (effectLayerTilemap)
$A8 keeps the entry's byte offset so AdvanceEventRow can reload the start X coordinates.

=== TILE COPY OPERATIONS ===

1. CopyEventBlockTiles (instant): nested row/column loop using map_coords.MapIndexMoveRight/MapIndexMoveDown. Layer 0 copies the mapLayerTilemap and collisionLayer bytes. Layer 1 copies effectLayerTilemap and looks the collision byte up through the [$3E] pointer (base $06AC, low byte replaced by the tile ID, bank $7F); the collision byte is written only when the lookup is non-zero.

2. AnimateEventBlock (animated): same copy, but each copied tile that is inside the camera window also queues a 2×2 metatile VRAM update. Layer 0 queues through QueueVisibleTileVram (BG1 nametable) and, when the queue is full, flushes inside the routine (UpdateFrameDialogue) and restarts; layer 1 has its own inline copy of the visibility and queue code (BG2 nametable, $0800 offset) and instead returns carry clear when the queue is full so the caller (COP #33) flushes a frame and calls again. Carry set = all tiles done.

=== VRAM WRITE QUEUE ($0800-$08FF) ===

A queue entry is a pair of words (VRAM word address, tile word); one 2×2 metatile is four entries = $10 bytes, so the queue holds 16 metatiles (Y = $0100 = full). The queue's first word is dmaSkipFlag ($0800): nonzero means entries are pending. A zero address word terminates the list; both animate paths write that terminator at $0800+Y.
FlushVramWriteQueue (called twice from system_core's frame update) has two modes:
- Queued mode (dmaSkipFlag nonzero): SP is pointed at $07FF so PLA pops address/tile pairs straight into VMADDL/VMDATAL until the zero terminator; dmaSkipFlag is cleared afterwards.
- Direct mode (dmaSkipFlag zero): if tileQueryResult ($0902, really the VRAM address of a pending 2×2 metatile update staged by cop_handlers_metatile) is nonzero, writes its two tile rows ($0904/$0906 at $0902, $090A/$090C at $0908), then clears it.

=== VISIBILITY CHECK ===

A tile is queued only when its pixel position is inside the camera window: (pixelX + 16 − scrollH) < $0111 and (pixelY − ((scrollV − 16) AND $FFF0)) in 0..$F0. Layer 0 and QueueVisibleTileVram use bg1ScrollH / mapScrollV; the layer 1 path uses effectScrollH / effectScrollV.
QueueVisibleTileVram contract: carry set = off-screen (nothing queued); carry clear and Z set = queue full (the LDX #0 exists only to force Z); carry clear on success, where Z is whatever the caller's flags were (PLP restores them). DrawChestTiles in warps_interaction is its other caller and ignores the result.

=== HELPER ROUTINES ===

AdvanceEventColumn: decrements the column counter ($9E); carry set when the row is done, otherwise pixel X += 16, source/destination tile X += 1 and both map indices step right.
AdvanceEventRow: decrements the row counter ($A0); carry set when all rows are done, otherwise pixel Y += 16, tile Y += 1 (both), source X and destination X are reloaded from the original table entry ($A8) and the column counter is reset from $A2.
hardware_math:
Hardware math utilities — SNES multiplication and division using the 5A22 math registers (163840–164464, Bank 02).

Wrappers around the hardware multiplier ($4202/$4203 → $4216/$4217, unsigned 8×8) and divider ($4204/$4205/$4206 → $4214/$4216, unsigned 16÷8). Results need NOP delays (8 machine cycles after a multiply, 16 after a divide).

=== ROUTINES ===

MulDivide: (A low × Y) ÷ A high. A low = multiplier, A high = divisor, Y = 16-bit multiplicand. Two 8×8 multiplies (A low × Y low, A low × Y high) are combined into the 16-bit dividend: the product's low 16 bits only — anything above bit 15 is discarded, so the product must fit in 16 bits. A divisor of 0 gives $FFFF. Returns the 16-bit quotient. Users: camera_scroll, scanline_band_hdma_thinker, layer1_scroll_actors.

Multiply8x8Unsigned: 8×8 multiply with the operands in the two bytes of A (low = first, high = second), through long addresses ($80:4202/4203/4216/4217) so any data bank works. Returns the 16-bit product in A. The hardware multiplier is unsigned, so this is an unsigned multiply (Multiply8x8Unsigned). Used for index × $30 actor addressing, map index calculation, orbital offsets and others.

UnsignedDivide: 16÷8 divide. Y = 16-bit dividend, A = 8-bit divisor. Returns the quotient's low byte in A low and the remainder in A high (the quotient's high byte is dropped).

SoftDivide_Unused: software long division, no callers.

RngStep_Unused: standalone copy of the generator step that RngByte (cop_handlers_movement) runs inline; no callers.
inventory_menu:
Inventory menu UI system — full-screen inventory overlay with tab navigation, item management, and status display (189334–191746, Bank 02).

Implements the complete pause-menu inventory as an actor-def (InventoryMenuDef). The menu spawns 16 child actors for item slots, plus cursor, equipped-item display, and status row actors. Four tabs provide different inventory functions, each with its own input loop and display configuration.

=== ARCHITECTURE ===

InventoryMenuInit spawns all child actors in a loop (16 InventorySlotActors, plus EquipCursorActor, EquippedItemDisplay, StatusAbilityRow0/1/2) and saves their actor indices in long-address scratch fields:
  orbitAngle ($7F0010,X) = first slot actor Y index (linked list head)
  orbitDiameter ($7F0012,X) = equip cursor actor Y index
  moveXAlt ($7F0018,X) = equipped item display actor Y index
  moveYAlt ($7F001A,X) = last status row actor Y index (chain head)

The main loop (InventoryMainLoop) runs TabSelectionLoop for tab navigation. Tab changes dispatch to TabHover* routines (preview) via SwitchCase on TabHoverDispatch. Tab confirmation dispatches to TabAction* routines via TabActionDispatch.

=== BUTTONS AND FRAME MODEL (this baserom) ===

BranchIfPressed tests joypadCurrent, the remapped logical bits. The menu uses two face-button bits: $8000 = confirm, $4000 = cancel. The baserom remap defaults (db-us/transforms.json) give physical A the value $8080, physical B $4008, X $0004, Y $0040 and Select $2000, so A confirms, B cancels, and X and Y are software-only bits that the menu ignores (except the widened swap mask, see ArrangePickTarget). A test with $C000 (UseItemTab, StatusViewTab) accepts A or B; the tab bar cancels on $6000 (B or Select). The diary menu can rebind the buttons, and the vanilla ROM tests different masks.

Consumption: TSB $joypadHeld masks the given bits out of joypadCurrent until the physical button is released. The code consumes exactly the bit it matched, so a consume of $8000 leaves the $0080 half of A's value visible (never tested here). A D-pad consume is wider than its direction: Up consumes $0B00 (Up, Left and Right) and Down consumes $0700 (Down, Left and Right), so one diagonal press moves one step; Left ($0200) and Right ($0100) consume only themselves.

Frame model: every handler is a COP script that yields with SetEntryHereAndYield / SetEntryHere + RTL and resumes at the saved entry point next frame. An RTL is therefore the idle path of a frame, never "exit the menu". The menu closes when TabCancel sets exit flag byte #00, which the main loop of inventory_overlay polls.

=== TAB SYSTEM (4 tabs) ===

0 = Use: Equip/unequip items. 4×4 grid cursor ($1A = slot index). A or B ($C000) confirms the cursor slot as the equipped item; confirming an empty slot clears the equipment ($FFFF). Entering the tab first writes inventoryEquippedIndex = 0 (a non-negative placeholder that lets ShowEquipCursor reveal the cursor); UseItemConfirm always overwrites it, because the tab can only end through the confirm. The tab title string reads "Gather Items".

1 = Arrange: Swap items between slots. Two-phase: A picks the source slot ($22; B leaves the tab), then a second cursor picks the target (the source moves to $2E/$2C, the target cursor uses $22/$20; B cancels only the target). ArrangePerformSwap does an 8-bit byte swap in inventorySlots, updates both slot actor sprites via UpdateSlotActorSprite, and tries to keep inventoryEquippedIndex on the moved item. Only the case "the source slot was equipped" works: the case "the target slot was equipped" compares a slot actor address with a slot index and can never match (see the ArrangePerformSwap part note). Swapping a slot with itself is ignored.

2 = Discard: Remove items. Grid cursor selects a slot; CheckItemDiscardable gates via a bitfield table (BitMaskTable × system_strings.non_discardable_item_bits). If discardable, YesNoPromptLoop asks "Discard? No / Yes" with the cursor on No ($28 = 0); only $28 = 1 (Yes) discards. On yes: zeroes the slot's item byte (AND #$FF00 on a 16-bit read/write: slots are single bytes, so the high byte is the NEXT slot, written back unchanged), updates the sprite, clears the equip state if the equipped item was discarded. Empty slots and protected items play SFX #12 instead.

3 = Status: View character abilities. 3-row vertical cursor ($22 = 0/1/2). For each row, TestAbilityFlag checks whether the ability is unlocked for the current characterForm. Unlocked abilities show their name via ComputeAbilityIndex → RunBg3Script. The rows are the first three ability flags of the CURRENT form (row r tests flag $0510 + characterForm×4 + r, the same flags as abilityBitmask $0AA2); the form's fourth ability flag is never listed. A or B ($C000) leaves the tab.

=== MYSTIC STATUE PEDESTALS ===

The inventory menu does NOT spawn or manage the mystic statue pedestal actors directly. Six inventory_statue_slot actors (Bank 00) are spawned independently by SpawnSceneActors from the scene $FF actor list. They share the screen with the inventory menu but operate as autonomous actors.

The pedestals are arranged symmetrically around the 4×4 item grid: 3 on the left (X ~24–40) and 3 on the right (X ~200–216), at three vertical positions (Y ~48, ~88, ~136). Each pedestal checks one of six event flags ($F8–$FD at $0A1F) via TestFlagRaw. If the flag is set (statue collected), the pedestal shows its inventory_spritemap sprite ($3A–$3F). If not set, the actor immediately dies (no display).

The statues auto-hide when inventoryTabIndex == 3 (Status tab) and show on all other tabs (Use/Arrange/Discard), matching the item grid visibility.

Flags are set by the statue_inventory_reward ceremony (scene $FD), triggered after defeating bosses:
  $F8 = Gold Ship event, $F9 = Viper (Sky Garden), $FA = Vampires (Mu),
  $FB = Sand Fanger (Great Wall), $FC = Mummy Queen (Pyramid), $FD = Olman (Babel Tower).

See inventory_statue_slot and statue_inventory_reward block notes (Bank 00) for complete data flow.

=== GRID LAYOUT ===

16 inventory slots arranged in a 4×4 grid. Slot index bits: low 2 bits = column (0-3), bits 2-3 = row (0-3). GridColumnPositions provides X positions for columns ($005C, $0074, $008C, $00A4). Y position = row × $10 + base ($0030 for grid, $0031 for slot actors). SlotPositionTable stores all 16 pre-computed screen positions.

Grid cursor navigation (GridCursorUp/Down/Left/Right): ±4 for vertical (skip one row = 4 columns), ±1 for horizontal, all AND $000F for wrapping. Left/Right do not wrap inside a row: column 3 + 1 lands on column 0 of the NEXT row and slot 15 + 1 wraps to slot 0 (the vertical moves wrap inside their column).

=== CURSOR BLINK ===

Both TabSelectionLoop and YesNoPromptLoop implement a frame-counter blink:
  $1C increments each frame. Bits 0-3 ($000F): non-zero → skip draw/clear.
  Bit 4 ($0010): 0 → draw cursor, 1 → clear cursor.
  Result: cursor toggles visibility every 16 frames.

Tab cursor writes tile $202B (arrow glyph) to BG3 tilemap at $7F0200 + computed offset. Clear writes a blank tile to all 4 tab cursor positions (tile $2060 in this baserom; db-us/transforms.json rewrites the vanilla constant). YesNo cursor uses the same pattern at different offsets.

=== ACTOR VISIBILITY ===

Actor flag bit 13 ($2000) in actor+$0010 controls render visibility: SET = hidden, CLEAR = visible.

The menu actor's own DP $10 bit $1000 means "the 16 item slots are visible": set by InventoryMenuInit and ShowAllItemSlots, cleared by HideAllItemSlots. Both routines test it first, so repeated hover previews cost nothing.

=== ITEM DATA MODEL ===

inventorySlots ($0AB4): 16 bytes, one item ID per slot (0 = empty), no per-slot flags. Code reads a slot as a 16-bit word and masks it (AND #$00FF); the high byte of that word is the next slot.
inventoryEquippedIndex ($0AC4): Slot index of equipped item ($FFFF = nothing equipped).
inventoryEquippedType ($0AC6): Item type ID of equipped item.
itemAbilityIndex ($0AE8): Set before RunBg3Script to display item/ability descriptions.
characterForm ($0AD4): Current character (0=Will, 1=Freedan, 2=Shadow) — affects status abilities.

=== ABILITY SYSTEM ===

ComputeAbilityIndex: Maps (characterForm, abilitySlot) → global ability index = characterForm × 4 + slot + 1. Stored to itemAbilityIndex for description display.

TestAbilityFlag: Maps (characterForm, abilitySlot) → game flag index = characterForm × 4 + slot, calls TestFlag_0510. Returns carry set if the ability is unlocked (the current form is passed in $0004, not read from characterForm).

CheckItemDiscardable: Tests item ID against a bitfield at system_strings.non_discardable_item_bits (the 8 bytes are a "non-discardable items" bit table). Item ID >> 3 = byte index, item ID & 7 = bit via BitMaskTable. Returns carry set if item is non-discardable (quest item).
inventory_overlay:
Inventory screen overlay: full scene save / restore around the pause-menu inventory (191746-192584, Bank 02).

The inventory is a normal scene ($FF) with its own actors and thinkers that reuses the live WRAM. OpenInventoryScreen therefore saves the pools and state it will overwrite, builds scene $FF, runs UpdateFrameDialogue until the inventory_menu actor sets flag byte #00, restores everything and reloads the previous scene's graphics. Called through JSL from GlobalInputHandler (Select). Not saved: tile / map data (the scene script reloads it), VRAM (reloaded), sprite VRAM tiles for the player and ability effects (reloaded explicitly).

=== SAVE MAP (SaveGameState / RestoreGameState) ===

map_coords:
Map coordinate utilities (Bank 02): tile and pixel coordinates to map indices and BG1 VRAM addresses, map index stepping, and the two slope probes used by player movement.

=== Map index format ===
The map is a grid of 16x16-tile pages of 256 bytes, row-major, with a per-layer page stride (mapRowStrideL0/L1, $0693/$0695, selected by X = 0 or 2). index = (((tileY >> 4) x stride + (tileX >> 4)) << 8) or ((tileY and $F) << 4) or (tileX and $F). The same index addresses mapLayerTilemap ($7EA000), the collision map ($7FC000; an index at or above $4000 is out of range) and the effect layer.
- TileCoordsToMapIndex: DP $18/$1C (tile X/Y), X = layer selector -> X = index. Multiply8x8Unsigned multiplies the stride (A low) by the page row (A high = tileY >> 4). 16 JSL sites in warps_interaction, event_blocks, cop_handlers_metatile and cop_handlers_collision.
- PixelToVramAddress: DP $1A/$1E (pixel X/Y) -> A = ((Y and $F8) << 2) + ((X and $F8) >> 3) + ((X and $100) << 2) + $1000: the BG1 nametable (64x32 words at VRAM $1000, second 32x32 half for X bit 8; X wraps at 512 px and Y at 256 px). event_blocks adds $0800 for BG2.
- MapIndexMoveRight/Left/Down/Down_L1 step the index kept in $02 by one cell and return it in X. Right and both Down variants also store it back in $02; MapIndexMoveLeft returns X only. MapIndexMoveDown_L1 loads $02 without a REP, so it relies on the caller's M width (its two callers in event_blocks have M = 16).

=== Slope probes ===
FindSlopeForWestMove and FindSlopeForEastMove have exactly one caller each: DispatchWestMove (player_move_west) calls FindSlopeForWestMove and DispatchEastMove (player_move_east) calls FindSlopeForEastMove. They are interleaved with the coordinate code only because they share its tile_collision helpers. Both look for the slope collision types $0A (east-facing) and $05 (west-facing) at the corner probe, at the cell one ROW up (only after a transition tile) and one ROW down (MapCellUp/MapCellDown on the index in $00), then at two future-position corners (ProbeFutureTL/BL for the right probe, TR/BR for the left one).
Return convention (callers test Z first): Z set = a slope was found, with carry clear for $0A and carry set for $05; Z clear = nothing found. The callers branch BNE (none), then BCS ($05: WestRampUp / WestRampDescend) or fall through ($0A: EastRampDown / WestRampAscend). The old 'carry clear when found' header was wrong. The probe pixel X in $1A is modified in place (+8 for the right probe, -8 for the left one).

1. MusicJingleActor saves musicParentActor ($06F2, the scene's current music index) in orbitAngle
2. Spawns SpcTransferMusicData with chatPtr = $26 + 1 (music data index of the jingle) and flags it $1000

MusicRenderSync does WaitByte #48 (73 ticks), clears its own $1000 flag, zeros joypadMaskStd, sets DBR to the string bank ($22), then calls UpdateFrameRender and DialogStringRenderer (Y = $20) once to show the string, and dies.

=== ACTOR POOL GUARD ===

Both SpawnAfterFlags calls check for a $1FC0 return (actor pool exhausted). On failure MusicLoadCleanup clears displayModeFlags bit 7 and kills the actor, so the music load is abandoned gracefully.

=== QUERY INTERFACE ===

IsMusicPlaying: returns carry set while musicTransitionState is nonzero or displayModeFlags bit 7 is set, carry clear otherwise. Used by melody items, the global input handler and several NPC scripts to avoid starting new music or input while a jingle sequence is active.
player_character:
Main player character actor definition and movement state machine (181132–184272).

This is the largest player actor file — the actor-def that instantiates the player and contains the complete movement FSM, traversal systems (climbing, ladders, shimmy), combat (melee, run attack, lunge), and related helpers. The actor-def's init code spawns four companion actors: attack_ability_system (charged attacks), player_move_controller (per-frame physics), slope_ramp_physics (slope tile handling), and shadow_shimmer (Shadow's palette shimmer).

=== BUTTON AND FLAG CONVENTIONS USED IN THIS FILE ===
Logical button masks (after the remap): attack $0080, use-item $0008, L $0020, R $0010 (L/R together $0030), D-pad $0F00 (R $0100, L $0200, Dn $0400, Up $0800). BranchIfPressed/BranchIfNotPressed take a mask word: bit 0 clear tests joypadCurrent (held buttons minus the ones consumed in joypadHeld or hidden by joypadMaskStd), bit 0 set tests joypadRaw (no consumption, no masking). TSB joypadHeld therefore CONSUMES a button (joypadCurrent stops reporting it); it does not inject one. TSB joypadMaskStd with $CFFC hides everything except Start/Select ($3000) and bits 0-1 from joypadCurrent, D-pad included; the ladder and shimmy code reads Up/Down through joypadRaw masks such as $0801 / $0401.
Actor flag word $10 (this file): $0008 normal collision-aware movement (cleared while climbing, restored on exit), $0020 block marker (set by the block loop, cleared by PlayerIdleEntry), $0080 hit-reaction counter active (actor_execution), $0200 set while the Psycho Slider and the lunge run, $4000 off-screen (set by sprite_composition). The meaning of $0100 and $2000 for the player is not traced.

1. CORE IDLE + WALKING (181132–181790)

A walk entered while the player already faces that way (PlayerIdleEntry leaves the facing index in $24) with the window still open ($040C >= 0) closes the window, sets the axis speed to ±3 and yields once before re-dispatching: a run start. docs/ram_map.txt describes $040C the same way ("running-allowed timer"); the invincibilityTimer mnemonic name is stale. player_move_controller:
Player movement integrator (Bank 02, 176798-177195): the per-frame companion actor that turns the player's velocity inputs into a new position.

SPAWN AND ORDER: PlayerCharacterDef spawns it with SpawnAfter. Every SpawnAfter inserts the new actor directly behind its spawner, and slope_ramp_physics is spawned after this actor, so the actor list reads attack_ability_system, player, slope_ramp_physics, this controller. The slope code has therefore already edited playerSpeedEw / playerSpeedNs when this runs in the same frame. CopyActorState sets the hidden bit ($2000) on it, so only its script runs.

STATE: this actor's own $14 / $16 hold the player's position in SUB-PIXELS (4 per pixel, 2 fractional bits). The x4 scaling at the top runs once, when the actor spawns; every later frame resumes after SetEntryHere. The player actor's $0014 / $0016 stay in plain pixels (the write-back stores sub-pixels >> 2).

PER FRAME:
1. HIT-STUN: if the player's $10 has bit $0080 (the iframe counter is running) and iframeCounter is not negative, skip the frame. A positive counter is hit-stun, so this is the check that freezes the player (actor_execution exempts the player from its own freeze); a negative counter (recovery) lets movement continue.
2. LOCK: if playerFlags has EITHER bit $0200 (game over) or $0800 (script / ability lock) set, clear extVelocityX / Y and skip: the script or the traversal code (stairs, vine, ladder, cutscene) owns the position.
3. SYNC: if the player actor's pixel position differs from local >> 2 (a script or COP moved the player), adopt the actor's position x4; the old fraction is lost.
4. VELOCITY, per axis. Speed word (playerSpeedEw / playerSpeedNs) zero: joypad velocity from JoypadToVelocity plus the external velocity; the joypad part is forced to zero while playerFlags has $1000 (on-slope latch) or $2000 (guard / channel stance). Speed nonzero: speed x 4 plus the external velocity, and the $1000 latch is cleared. One speed unit is one pixel per frame; the joypad gives +/-8 sub-pixels (2 px per frame).
5. MOVE: bit $0008 of the player actor's $10 means 'collision-checked movement' (actor_execution uses the same bit for every actor). Set: player_move_main.PlayerMovementTick runs the tile collision with X = THIS actor's slot, positions in the low-RAM words $22 / $26 and velocities in $20 / $24. Clear (the vine, ladder and shimmy states clear it and restore it on exit): the velocity is added to the position with no collision.
6. WRITE-BACK: local position = $22 / $26; the player actor gets position >> 2; bit $0004 (solid contact, set by the tick in this actor's own $10) is copied into the player's $10.

External velocities ($0408 / $040A) are consumed (zeroed) every frame, so a source must write them every frame to keep pushing: av71_wind_effect, btEA_conveyor_controller, combat_collision (push hits), gw82_archer, sg55_viper. scene_lifecycle clears them and both speed words at scene setup.
JoypadToVelocity (end of file) is called only from here.
player_move_east:
East (positive $20) horizontal-phase collision dispatch, east wall-slide handlers and the Y auto-align (186076-186435 + 187085-187264, Bank 02). DispatchEastMove is called once per tick by PlayerMovementTick after $AA bit $0040 is set. It is the mirror image of DispatchWestMove (player_move_west, the WEST half) and probes the right-hand corners (TR / BR) where the west file probes TL / BL. The slope handlers it jumps to live in player_move_ramps.

=== CONVENTIONS ===

As in player_move_ns: sub-pixels (4 per pixel), $20 / $22 = X velocity / position, $24 / $26 = Y velocity / position (Y grows downward), $1A / $1E = probe pixel, $00 = map index of the last probe (X still holds it right after a probe), CheckSubTileAlignX / Y carry clear = flush on a 16-px line, carry set = straddling two cells. $06 / $09 are undecoded wall-like types, so 'north wall' / 'south wall' are handler names. In this phase the vertical velocity is parked on PlayerMovementTick's stack and $24 is 0, so the SnapYNorthCollision / SnapYSouthCollision calls here work on the CURRENT Y, not a stepped one.

=== DISPATCH ORDER (DispatchEastMove) ===

1. map_coords.FindSlopeForEastMove: slope search at the hitbox centre column (the TR probe X minus 8, i.e. X itself; not a sample 8 px to the left). Z set = slope found: carry set = $05 -> WestRampUp, carry clear = $0A -> EastRampDown.
2. ProbeCurrentTR $09 -> EastWallPushDown; ProbeCurrentBR $06 -> EastWallPushUp.
3. ProbeFutureTR: $0E and above -> blocked path; $09 -> EastWallNorthFlag.
4. CheckSubTileAlignY. Y flush: future TR $06 -> EastWallSouthFlag, anything else on to step 5. Y straddling: future TR $06 -> blocked path; otherwise the cell below the future TR cell (MapCellDown) is read: $0E and above -> blocked, $06 -> EastWallSouthFlag, $09 -> blocked, anything else on to step 5 with A = that lower cell's type.
5. A = $07 -> EastLadderTile (A is the future TR type when Y is flush and the lower cell's type when Y straddles). Then ProbeCurrentBL: $05 -> WestRampDown, $0A -> EastRampUp.
6. Otherwise $22 += $20.

Blocked path (loc_02D753): SetActorCollisionFlag, AutoAlignNS_East (Y nudge, carry clear = nudged), then SnapXEastCollision. After a nudge the X snap runs without zeroing playerSpeedEw, so the player keeps pushing east and is walked around the corner.

SnapXEastCollision: X' = (((X + $20) - 32) AND $FFC0) + 32 (the second $20 is the immediate constant): the column of the stepped left edge, centred, so the right edge (X + 7 px) ends on the last pixel of that column, flush to the wall. With $20 = 0 (the callers in player_move_ns and player_move_south) it only moves X west. It zeroes $20; the full entry also zeroes playerSpeedEw.

=== WALL-SLIDE HANDLERS ===

EastWallPushDown (current TR $09, or future TR $09 through EastWallNorthFlag) and EastWallPushUp (current BR $06, or future BR $06 through EastWallSouthFlag) mirror code_02DC4B and code_02DC9F of the west file. They set $AB bit 7 (the Flag entries set bit 2 / bit 3 instead); nothing reads those bits. The probe at the future corner plus CheckSubTileAlignX picks the path. X STRADDLING and the corner type matches ($09 / $06): gap chain. X flush, or another type: SnapYNorthCollision / SnapYSouthCollision first (with $24 = 0: the north snap moves the player DOWN to the next row line, 1..16 px; the south snap floors Y, up to 15 px north), then the corner is re-probed: clear or the same type -> the slide, anything else -> SnapXEastCollision + ApplyMovementDeltas.

Gap chains. North (loc_02D7AB): MapCellDown from the future TR cell must be empty or $0A, then MapCellLeft from that cell must be empty or $09. South (loc_02D7FF): MapCellUp from the future BR cell must be empty or $05, then MapCellLeft must be empty or $06. A failed test goes to ClearSpeedEW_5 / _6 (playerSpeedEw = 0, no position applied this tick). Both pass: ComputeEastSnapOffset, then WallSlidePushDown (north handler) or WallSlidePushUp (south handler).

Push direction: WallSlidePushDown stores a positive $24 and WallSlidePushUp a negative one (player_move_west) and ApplyMovementDeltas adds $24 to Y, so the $09 handler pushes the player SOUTH and the $06 handler pushes NORTH. Read together with the west file: TL $06 and TR $09 both push south, BL $09 and BR $06 both push north.

=== AutoAlignNS_East / ComputeEastSnapOffset ===

AutoAlignNS_East returns carry set (no nudge) when the vertical velocity word parked at $06,S is nonzero, when the collision byte at the last probe index carries an actor solid mark (high nibble), or when n = (($26 >> 2) AND $0F) is 0. For n >= 4 it nudges Y south ($26 += 8 sub-pixels, clamped at the next row line) if FutureBR is below $0E; failing that, for n <= 10, it nudges north ($26 -= 8, clamped at the row line) if FutureTR is below $0E. So n = 1..3 can only go north, 4..10 prefers south, 11..15 can only go south.

ComputeEastSnapOffset: $02 = ($1A AND $0F), plus $10 on the wall path when this step moves the probe across a 16-px column line (bit 4 of $1A XOR ($1A - $20 / 4)). The wall path is taken when the current TR is $09, or when Y straddles and the cell below the current TR is $06; otherwise $02 = $1A AND $0F alone. WallSlidePushDown / WallSlidePushUp add a Y-derived offset to $02 and, above $10, push Y by (total AND $0F) pixels.

Everything here is UNVERIFIED-RUNTIME (no emulator trace); the arithmetic is read from the code.
player_move_main:
Player movement tick and collision helpers (184272-185206, Bank 02). PlayerMovementTick is the collision-checked movement entry; the other routines are the shared helpers of the north / south / east / west handlers (player_move_ns, player_move_south, player_move_east, player_move_west).

=== ENTRY CONTRACT ===

PlayerMoveController (actors/player/player_move_controller) calls it with JSL once per frame when the player actor's flags word ($10) has bit $0008 set (collision-checked movement; the vine, ladder and shimmy states clear it, and then the controller adds the velocity to the position directly, with no collision). X at entry is the CONTROLLER's own actor slot: the tick saves it in the absolute scratch word $000A, and SetActorCollisionFlag later ORs bit $0004 (solid contact this tick) into that slot's $10; the controller copies the bit into the player's $10 when it writes the position back. The tick itself starts by clearing bit $0004 there.

D is set to $0000 for the whole tick, so the 2-digit operands below are low-RAM scratch words: $20 / $22 = X velocity / position, $24 / $26 = Y velocity / position, all in sub-pixels (4 per pixel, Y grows downward; the controller scaled the position by 4 before the call and wrote them to $22 / $26), $1A / $1E = the last probe's pixel X / Y, $00 / $02 / $04 = scratch, $AA / $AB = per-tick flag words (cleared together). The reference point of the 16x16 hitbox is the centre of its bottom edge.

=== TWO PHASES ===

1. Horizontal: the vertical velocity $24 is parked on the stack and zeroed. $20 = 0 skips the phase. Otherwise $AA bit $0040 is set (see below) and DispatchWestMove (negative $20) or DispatchEastMove (positive $20) runs. Afterwards $22 >> 2 and $26 >> 2 are stored in the player actor's pixel position ($0014 / $0016: the values are POSITIONS, not deltas) and $20 is cleared.
2. Vertical: the parked velocity is popped back into $24. Wall-slide handlers of the horizontal phase can zero the parked word (CancelVerticalPhase in player_move_west), which then cancels this phase. Zero skips it, negative runs DispatchNorthMove, positive runs DispatchSouthMove. The controller commits the final $22 / $26 after the tick returns.

$AA bits: $0040 = horizontal phase ran (read by AutoAlignEW_North here and AutoAlignEW_South, which refuse to nudge in that case). $0800 and $0400 are tested before the north and south dispatch, but nothing in extracted/ ever sets them; player_move_west only clears them (TRB #$0840 / #$0440). Those two gates therefore always pass. $AB bit 1 is set by DispatchWestMove and read by player_move_ns.

=== AutoAlignEW_North (north counterpart of AutoAlignEW_South) ===

Called only from the blocked path of DispatchNorthMove. Returns carry CLEAR when X was nudged by 2 pixels toward the open column, carry SET when nothing was done. Gates (carry set): $AA bit $0040, an actor solid mark in the collision byte at the map index left in X by the last probe (high nibble), or n = 0. n = (($22 >> 2) - 8) AND $0F is the offset of the hitbox's LEFT edge (X - 8) inside its 16-pixel column. n >= 6 tries an east nudge first: it needs ProbeFutureTR to return a type below $0E and not $06. If that fails (or n < 6) and n < 9, a west nudge is tried: ProbeFutureTL below $0E and not $09. So n = 1..5 can only go west, 6..8 prefers east, 9..15 can only go east.
Each nudge temporarily subtracts $20 sub-pixels (8 px) from $22 so that the helper tests the left edge, calls NudgeAxisPlus8Clamped (+8) or NudgeAxisMinus8Clamped (-8), then adds $20 back; the 2-pixel nudge itself stays in $22.

=== NUDGE HELPERS ===

Both work on the word at [$00 + X] (X = $22 for the X position, X = $26 for the Y position in player_move_east / player_move_west). NudgeAxisPlus8Clamped adds 8 sub-pixels (toward larger coordinates: east or south); if that crosses a $40 line (16 px) the result is floored to the line (AND #$FFC0), so the edge ends exactly flush. NudgeAxisMinus8Clamped subtracts 8 and, on crossing a $40 line, clamps back up to that line ((value AND #$FFC0) + $40). The 'lower' and 'upper' in the names refer to coordinate order, not to a screen direction.

=== ComputeYSnapOffset ===

$02 = 16 - (probe pixel Y AND $0F): the number of pixels to the next row line below, 1..16 ($10 when the probe is already flush). The computation is OR #$FFF0, EOR #$FFFF, INC. $1E is a pixel Y, not a sub-pixel position. Called from player_move_ns only (2 sites).

=== DiagSnapCompute_Unused ===

No reference anywhere in extracted/. It probes the current TL cell and takes the 'wall path' when the type is $06, or when X straddles two columns and the cell to the right is $09 (the same wall-like types as the north handlers). On the wall path $02 starts at 0; a nonzero $24 is converted to a pixel step ((>>2) OR #$C000 sign-extends only a NEGATIVE value, so it assumes a north move), negated, added to the saved Y, and if that crosses a 16-px line ($1E bit 4 changes) $02 = $10. The ComputeYSnapOffset formula for the current $1E is then added to $02. The probe coordinates $1A / $1E are saved and restored around the probe.

North (negative $24) vertical-phase collision dispatch, wall handlers and north slope physics (184376-184902, Bank 02). DispatchNorthMove is called once per tick by PlayerMovementTick after the horizontal phase; the mirror image for positive $24 is DispatchSouthMove in player_move_south.

=== CONVENTIONS ===

Positions are sub-pixels (4 per pixel; a 16-px tile is 64, so AND #$FFC0 floors to a row line). $24 / $26 are the Y velocity / position (negative = north, Y grows downward) and $22 is X. $1A / $1E are the probe pixel X / Y and $00 is the map index of the last probe; MapCellUp / Down / Left / Right read $00 and return the new index in X only (a caller that wants to keep it does STX $00; a result that is not stored is lost). CheckSubTileAlignX / Y: carry CLEAR = the probe sits on a 16-px line (flush), carry SET = it straddles two cells. Probe types: $02 ladder, $08 vine, $0E and above solid, $03 / $0C slopes; $06 / $09 are undecoded wall-like types, so 'south wall' / 'north wall' below are handler names, not directions.

=== DISPATCH ORDER (DispatchNorthMove) ===

1. ProbeCurrentTL (carry set only): $06 -> SouthWallHandler, $03 -> NorthSlopeRight, $0C -> NorthSlopeLeft; any other type falls on.
2. ProbeCurrentTR: $09 -> NorthWallHandler.
3. ProbeFutureTL (top-left after the step): $0E and above or $08 -> blocked path; $02 -> NorthInteractTile; $06 -> SouthWallNudge.
4. CheckSubTileAlignX. X flush: future TL $09 -> NorthProbeRedirect, anything else -> the plain step. X straddling: future TL $09 -> blocked path; otherwise MapCellRight (the future TR cell) is read: $0E and above, $08, $02 or $06 -> blocked path, $09 -> NorthProbeRedirect, anything else -> the plain step.
5. Plain step: $26 += $24 (Y shrinks). $22 and $20 are not touched; PlayerMovementTick commits the position afterwards.
6. Blocked path (loc_02D0AF): SetActorCollisionFlag, AutoAlignEW_North (nudge X onto the column grid, carry clear = nudged), then SnapYNorthCollision. After a nudge the Y snap runs without zeroing playerSpeedNs (entry loc_02D0C2), so the player keeps pushing and is walked around the corner a couple of pixels per tick.

=== SNAPPING ===

SnapYNorthCollision: Y' = $24 + $26 (the stepped Y), floored to a row line and moved one row down: $26 = (Y' AND $FFC0) + $40, $24 = 0. The hitbox top (feet - 16 px) then sits flush under the blocking row. In the normal blocked case Y' lies north of the old Y and the result falls between Y' and Y, so it backs the player off the step. Callers that run with $24 parked at 0 (the east and west wall-slide handlers) push the player SOUTH by 1..16 px instead (16 when already flush). The full entry also zeroes playerSpeedNs.

=== SLOPES ===

NorthSlopeRight ($03) and NorthSlopeLeft ($0C) are entered when the current TL has that type and need the current TR to match, else the move counts as blocked. The slope flag $09AF bit $10 (playerFlags $1000, on a slope) is set when Y is flush, when the cell below has the same type, or when d >= 8. Here d = 16 - n and n = (($26 + $24) >> 2) AND $0F is the row offset of the top probe inside the slope tile, so d >= 8 means the upper half of the tile; in the lower half (n >= 9, d < 8) the move is applied without the flag. The slope directions ('right' / 'left') are undecoded.

NorthSlopeLeft additionally filters the step through slopeFracAccum ($09C6, shared with the south handlers): a positive leftover is zeroed, then accum += $24. With |accum| >> 4 = 0 the unchanged $24 is applied and accum keeps the sum. Otherwise $24 is REPLACED by -(|accum| >> 4) and accum gains 16 per step. Nothing subtracts the distance that was actually moved, so for $24 = -8 the player alternates a full 2-px step and a 1-sub-pixel step (about 56 percent of the speed on average). UNVERIFIED-RUNTIME.

=== WALL HANDLERS ===

SouthWallHandler (current TL $06) and NorthWallHandler (current TR $09): if the opposite bottom corner (BR / BL) has the same type the player is enclosed and ClearMovementDeltas runs. Otherwise the future corner is probed and CheckSubTileAlignY decides. Y STRADDLING and future type $06 / $09: gap chain. Y flush, or another type: the snap path.
Gap chain: the neighbour cell east (SouthWallHandler, MapCellRight) or west (NorthWallHandler, MapCellLeft) of the future corner cell and the cell below that neighbour must both be type 0, else ClearSpeedNS_1 / _2 (playerSpeedNs = 0, nothing applied this tick). Both empty: ComputeYSnapOffset, then FineAdjustXWest / FineAdjustXEast. FineAdjustXWest moves X EAST and FineAdjustXEast moves X WEST (the names refer to the wall side), so SouthWallHandler slides the player east and NorthWallHandler west.
Snap path: SnapXWestCollision (SouthWallHandler: X to the centre of the next column east, also zeroes playerSpeedEw) or SnapXEastCollision (NorthWallHandler: X floored to its column centre, i.e. west), then the future corner is re-probed. Still $06 / $09: take the slide. Anything else: zero $24 (so SnapYSouthCollision floors the CURRENT Y with no step added) and apply the move.

SouthWallNudge (future TL $06): $AB bit 1 is set by DispatchWestMove in every tick where the west horizontal phase ran (a negative $20) and is cleared together with $AA at the start of the tick. If it is set and X is flush, the north step is cancelled ($24 = 0) and the X move is applied. Otherwise MapCellRight from the future TL cell: $0E and above -> zero $24 + SnapYSouthCollision + apply (loc_02D1BC); anything else -> the SouthWallHandler gap chain.

NorthProbeRedirect: reached from DispatchNorthMove when future TL is $09 (X flush) or the east cell is $09. Its MapCellDown + ReadCollisionNibble have no effect (MapCellDown only changes X, the nibble is dropped and MapCellLeft at loc_02D208 reads $00 again), so the chain starts from the cell recorded in $00.

Slope physics for eastward player movement (186435-187085, Bank 02). The four handlers are entered ONLY from DispatchEastMove (player_move_east); the west dispatcher (player_move_west) has its own ramp code (WestRampDescend and friends) and does not call here.

They call back into player_move_west (CancelVerticalPhase), player_move_east (EastWallNorthDiag / EastWallSouthDiag), player_move_south (SnapYSouthCollision) and player_move_ns (SnapYNorthCollision).

  EastRampDown : FindSlopeForEastMove found $0A (carry clear)
  WestRampUp   : FindSlopeForEastMove found $05 (carry set)
  EastRampUp   : ProbeCurrentBL read $0A (late path of DispatchEastMove)
  WestRampDown : ProbeCurrentBL read $05

Tile types: $0A (east-facing) is a surface that falls toward the east, Y grows with X; $05 (west-facing) rises toward the east. Both direct paths agree: $0A adds the X velocity to Y ($26 += $20), $05 subtracts it. 'Up' / 'Down' in the names is not the Y direction: EastRampUp's direct path also descends.

=== COORDINATES ===

$1A is the probe pixel X and $1E the probe pixel Y (tile_collision convention). '$1A -= 8' therefore moves the probe 8 px WEST; it does not move the probe in Y. ProbeCurrentTR leaves $1A = X + 8 and $1E = Y - 16 (hitbox top row); ProbeCurrentBR leaves $1A = X + 8 and $1E = Y (bottom + 1); ProbeCurrentBL leaves $1A = X - 8 and $1E = Y. The -8 / +8 therefore lands on the hitbox centre column X. FutureTR minus 9 is one pixel west of the post-step centre column.

=== COMMON FLOW ===

1. CancelVerticalPhase zeroes the word at $05,S, the vertical velocity PlayerMovementTick parked on its stack, so the NS phase later does nothing and these handlers own the Y movement.
2. Probe the slope type in several cells (listed in each handler note). No slope: the Redirect handlers (FutureTR $09 -> EastWallNorthDiag, FutureBR $06 -> EastWallSouthDiag) or ApplyMovementDeltas.
3. Slope found:
   - direct entries (the first samples hit the slope cell or the cell next to it, no crossing test): $26 -/+= $20, the X velocity copied 1:1 into Y (a 45-degree slope).
   - after the future probe: CheckTileBoundaryXor (Z clear = this step crosses a 16-px column line). No crossing: plain ApplyMovementDeltas. Crossing: n = ((X + step) in px) AND $0F, the pixels past the line. EastRampDown: $26 += 4n; WestRampUp: $26 -= 4n; then +4 / -4 (one pixel; positions are quarter pixels) when bit 2 of ($26 + $20 + $22) is set (a Y position plus X values, as in the original). EastRampUp / WestRampDown instead set $24 = $20 - 4n / 4n - $20, which ApplyMovementDeltas applies.
4. playerFlags |= $1000 (on slope / ramp), then the FutureTR and FutureBR wall check ($0E+ = solid): both open -> ApplyMovementDeltas; TR open and BR solid -> SnapYSouthCollision; TR solid and BR open -> SnapYNorthCollision; both solid -> corner snap.
5. Corner snap: X = (left edge of the post-step position, floored to a 16-px column line) + 8, so it only ever moves west; $26 += old X + $20 - new X (the distance pulled back); $20, $24 and playerSpeedEw are zeroed and SetActorCollisionFlag is called. The Y compensation has the same sign in the $0A and $05 handlers.

South (+Y) movement collision dispatch and grid alignment (185206-186076, Bank 02).

Entered from PlayerMovementTick (player_move_main) with $24 > 0, after the horizontal (EW) phase has run (so $20 is already zero), unless $AA bit $0400 is set (nothing sets it). Everything here works on sub-pixels (4 per pixel): $22/$26 are the X/Y position, $24 the Y velocity (positive = south, Y grows downward). A 16-pixel tile is 64 sub-pixels, so AND #$FFC0 floors to a tile line.

- Probe* routines (tile_collision) return A = collision type nibble and carry SET for any nonzero type, with the probed map index left in $00. Solid is A >= $0E, tested by the callers here.
- MapCellRight / MapCellLeft / MapCellUp read the index in $00 and return the neighbouring cell in X; the callers commit it with STX $00 before ReadCollisionNibble.
- CheckSubTileAlignX / Y: carry CLEAR = the probe edge is flush with a tile line (the hitbox covers a single column / row), carry SET = it straddles two cells. A is preserved.
- Types seen here: $02 ladder, $08 vine (can only be entered while walking south; the north dispatcher treats $08 as a wall), $03 / $0C slopes, $06 / $09 undecoded wall-like types. The 'North' / 'South' in SouthWallNorth* / SouthWallSouth* names comes from the type ($09 / $06), not from a direction.

  CurrentBL $09 -> SouthWallNorthInteract
  CurrentBL $03 -> SouthSlopeRight, $0C -> SouthSlopeLeft
  CurrentBR $06 -> SouthWallSouthInteract
  FutureBL >= $0E -> SouthBlockedWall
  FutureBL $02 -> SouthInteractTile (ladder), $08 -> SouthStairsTile (vine), $09 -> SouthWallNorthProbe
  Left column aligned: FutureBL $06 -> SouthSlideJumpShim, else a plain step
  Left column straddling two columns: FutureBL $06 blocks; then the cell to the right is tested ($0E+ / $02 / $09 block, $06 -> SouthSlideJumpShim)
  Otherwise: $26 += $24 (the step does not touch $22 and does not clear $24).

SouthBlockedWall first tries AutoAlignEW_South (a 2 px X nudge toward the open column). A nudge keeps playerSpeedNs, so the player keeps pushing and slides past the corner on the next tick; no nudge goes through SnapYSouthCollision, which zeroes playerSpeedNs. Both end in the shared floor ((Y + $24) AND $FFC0, then $24 = 0): the feet end flush against the top of the blocked row.

SouthSlopeRight ($03) and SouthSlopeLeft ($0C) require the matching type under both feet, otherwise SouthBlockedWall. The slope flag (playerFlags $1000, set through the high byte playerStateByte $09AF bit $10) is set when the feet are on a tile line, when the cell above is the same slope type, or when the row offset of the new Y is >= 8; only a misaligned player with a different cell above and an offset < 8 moves without it. Which diagonal each slope type follows is not decoded here.

If the opposite top corner is the same type the player is fully stopped (ClearMovementDeltas). Otherwise the handler probes the destination, tests the cells beside it, and either clears playerSpeedNs (ClearSpeedNS_3 / _4), floors Y, or takes the slide: ComputeSouthSnapOffset measures how far the step penetrates and FineAdjustXWest / FineAdjustXEast move X out of the wall.
