QuintetLzDecompress:
QuintetLZ decompression engine (164464–164770, Bank 02).

Implements the LZSS-variant compression algorithm used across Quintet (Enix) games — Illusion of Gaia, Soul Blazer, and Robotrek — for compressing graphics, tilemaps, and other data.

=== ALGORITHM ===
Dictionary-based compression with a 256-byte sliding window. A bitstream control layer determines token types:
- Bit = 1 → Literal: read 8 bits via LzReadBitField, write byte to output and dictionary
- Bit = 0 → Back-reference: read 8-bit dictionary index via LzReadBitField, then 4-bit length via LzReadNibble. Copy (length + 2) bytes from dictionary to both output and dictionary write position

The dictionary is initialized to $20 (space character), providing good compression for text-heavy data. The starting write position is $EF (DICTIONARY_OFFSET), matching the Quintet standard across all three games.

=== BITSTREAM FORMAT ===
Bits are read MSB-first within each source byte. DP $72 holds a one-hot mask of the NEXT unread bit, starting at $80 (bit 7). Each control bit consumed shifts the mask right via LSR. When the mask shifts out entirely (all 8 bits consumed), it resets to $80 via ROR and the source pointer [$3E] advances.

LzReadBitField (8-bit read) and LzReadNibble (4-bit read) use position cascades keyed on the mask. When the required bits straddle a byte boundary they read a 16-bit word from the source, XBA to swap byte order, and enter ASL (8-bit read) or LSR (4-bit read) fall-through cascades to align the result. In LzReadNibble the one-hot mask itself sits in the low byte of the 16-bit word and acts as the shift counter: LSR runs until the mask's single set bit is shifted out into carry.

=== WRAM LAYOUT ===
$3E/$3F/$40: 24-bit source pointer to compressed data (past the 2-byte size header). The routine advances $3E/$3F with 16-bit increments and never carries into the bank byte $40, so a stream must not cross a bank boundary; the pointer is left one past the last byte used.
$72: Bit mask — one-hot, MSB-first, resets to $80 on byte boundary
$74/$75: Dictionary write pointer (low byte = position within 256-byte page at $7E0200; the 8-bit INC wraps it inside the page)
$76/$77: Back-reference read pointer (same $02xx page; set per back-ref token)
$78/$79: Decompressed byte count (loaded into Y as countdown)
$7A/$7B: Output buffer address in bank $7E (loaded into X for STA $0000,X)
$7E0200–$7E02FF: 256-byte sliding dictionary. This page is also the first half of the depth-sort bucket array that sprite_composition's ClearActorRenderList zeroes ($0200–$03FE; mnemonic deathFlag = $0200), so every decompression leaves garbage there: callers must run ClearActorRenderList afterwards (the Decompress COP and the scene-load sequence do).

=== ENTRY CONDITIONS ===
Caller sets: [$3E] = source pointer (past size header), $78 = decompressed size (must be non-zero: a zero count runs for 65,536 bytes; scene_script skips size 0, the Decompress COP does not test it), $7A = output address within bank $7E (the data bank is set to $7E internally, so $7F output is impossible). X, Y, P and DBR are preserved across the call; A is not.

Reference: QuintetLZ class in @gaialabs/core (src/compression/QuintetLZ.ts).
scene_script:
Scene initialization script interpreter and graphics loading pipeline (164795–168078, Bank 02).

This is the scene setup engine — when the game transitions to a new area (map, dungeon room, cutscene backdrop, etc.), the scene script system reads byte-coded commands from scene data and executes them to configure the PPU display mode, load BG tile graphics, transfer tilemaps, set up map geometry, load sprite tiles, and transfer SPC music data.

=== ARCHITECTURE ===

The system centers on a command interpreter (SceneScriptMain) that reads one-byte opcodes from a scene script stream, dispatches them through a 24-entry jump table (scene_script_jump_table), and loops until opcode $00 (end-of-scene) is reached. SceneScriptNoMusic is a variant that filters out music load commands ($11) by skipping their operand bytes.

Scene script data is structured as: [scene_id:u16, command_stream...] entries. FindCurrentScene scans the table for a matching scene ID, then the interpreter processes commands sequentially using ReadScriptByte + Y-register stream position. The rebuilt tree finds scenes through scene_meta_list (indexed by scene id) via baserom/scene-load/SceneMetaLoad.patch.asm, which replaces FindCurrentScene and SkipScriptCommands with indexed lookups; the versions extracted here are the scanning originals.

=== COMMAND SET (scene_script_jump_table, 24 entries) ===

| Opcode | Handler | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| $02 | SceneCmd_ConfigDisplay | Configure PPU display mode from display_preset_table |
| $03 | SceneCmd_LoadBgTiles | Load BG tile graphics (2bpp/4bpp) with decompression |
| $04 | SceneCmd_LoadPalette | Load palette colours into the palette buffer cgramPalette ( < start, end, dest > ) |
| $05 | SceneCmd_LoadMetatileSets | Load metatile sets into WRAM for layer 0 and/or layer 1, then build the metatile flag table |
| $06 | SceneCmd_LoadLayerMaps | Load layer maps (width, height, compressed map) for layer 0 and/or layer 1; with no layer bit set, load a tileset to low VRAM |
| $0E | SceneCmd_Skip3 | Skip 3 bytes in script stream |
| $10 | SceneCmd_LoadSpriteTiles | Load sprite tile graphics |
| $11 | SpcMusicLoadCmd | Transfer SPC music data via APU handshake |
| $13 | SceneCmd_Branch | Conditional execution based on game flag |
| $14 | SceneCmd_Label | Label: no-op that skips its id byte; the position is what jump ($15) and branch ($13) continue at |
| $15 | SkipScriptCommands | Skip remaining commands in current scene block |
| $17 | SceneCmd_LoadCharTiles | Load character/object tiles with flexible VRAM targeting |

Opcodes $00-$01, $07-$0D, $0F, $12, $16 all map to SceneCmd_Default (RTS, no-op).

=== GRAPHICS PIPELINE ===

Scene commands use a shared pipeline for loading compressed tile data:
1. ReadScriptByte reads tile parameters (VRAM offset, size, flags)
2. LoadScriptPointer reads a 3-byte ROM pointer from the script stream
3. CheckSourceCacheHit compares against cached source addresses to skip redundant loads
4. If cache miss: QuintetLzDecompress decompresses to staging buffer ($7E:7000)
5. DMA transfer via DmaTileStripToVram or DmaRomToWram sends data to VRAM or WRAM
6. SaveVramToRingBuffer backs up VRAM contents for fast cache-hit restoration

Three tile data formats:
- Standard 2bpp/4bpp tiles (SceneCmd_LoadBgTiles mode 0)
- Full 4bpp page load (Load4bppPage, mode 3)
- Priority-interleaved tiles (DeinterleavePlanarTiles → InterleaveTilesPriority, used when layerPriorityFlag bit $0800 is set)

=== GRAPHICS CACHE SYSTEM ===

A 4-entry ring buffer cache (GraphicsCacheLookup/GraphicsCacheStore) tracks recently-loaded tile source addresses at $0084-$008F (3 bytes each: addr_lo, addr_hi, bank). On cache hit, RestoreCachedVram DMA-copies the previously-saved VRAM data from a WRAM ring buffer (4 × $2000 byte slots at $7F:4000-$7F:DFFF) back to VRAM — avoiding the expensive decompression step entirely.

SaveVramToRingBuffer reads current VRAM back to WRAM after each load, rotating through ring buffer slots via ComputeRingBufferAddr. For tile data exceeding $2000 bytes, two consecutive ring buffer slots are used.

A second, independent cache is the SOURCE-POINTER cache: ten 3-byte slots at $066C-$0689 (addr_lo, addr_hi, bank) remember which compressed source each command last loaded. CheckSourceCacheHit(X = slot) returns carry clear when the pointer in $3E/$40 matches the slot (skip the load) and otherwise stores the new pointer. Slots: $066C/$066F/$0672/$0675 = BG tiles (mode 0/1 by flag bit 4), $0678/$067B = dual-tilemap layers 0/1, $067E/$0681 = FullGraphics layers 0/1, $0684 = sprite tiles, $0687 = SPC music. Code invalidates a slot by zeroing its high byte + bank (`STZ slot+1`, 16-bit), which makes the next lookup a guaranteed miss.

Scratch used by every loader: $0664 = source window start, $0666 = source window end (DMA size = end - start, source = $3E + start), $0668 = destination (VRAM page = word address >> 8, or WRAM offset), $066A = layer/target flags from the script.

=== MAP GEOMETRY ===

SceneCmd_LoadLayerMaps handles complete scene setup including map dimensions:
- Reads width ($00/$01) and height ($02/$03) from script data
- StoreMapAndDecompress sets map row stride, computes total map byte count via Multiply8x8Unsigned, and decompresses tilemap data to the layer's tilemap base address
- WriteMapBounds stores computed dimensions to mapBoundsX/mapBoundsY for the camera system
- Dual-layer support: flag bit 0 selects layer 0 (primary tilemap at $7E:A000), flag bit 1 selects layer 1 (overlay at $7E:C000); bit 7 alone means "tileset only" (DmaLowVramTileset)

=== TILEMAP ATTRIBUTE SYSTEM ===

BuildMetatileFlagTable post-processes a loaded metatile definition table (4 tilemap words per metatile). For each metatile it lifts bit 9 out of the four words, clears it, merges the layer's priority/offset word ($06A2+X), and packs the four lifted bits into one flag byte in a bank-$7F table. RebuildCollisionLayer then uses that table, indexed by each map cell's metatile number, to fill the collision layer ($7F:C000).

BuildAttributeTable creates a lookup table mapping metatile indices to their attribute bytes, referenced during deinterleaved tile rendering.

=== PPU DISPLAY CONFIGURATION ===

SceneCmd_ConfigDisplay reads a display_preset_table index and configures 10 PPU-related fields: TM/TS (main/sub screen designation), TMW/TSW (window masks), CGWSEL/CGADSUB (color math), layerPriorityFlag, scrollModeFlags, BGMODE, and BG tilemap addresses (BG1SC/BG2SC). The layerPriorityFlag bit 7 swaps BG1/BG2 tilemap base address assignment between $10xx and $18xx.

=== SPC MUSIC LOADING ===

SpcMusicLoadCmd implements the full SPC700 IPL transfer protocol: Wait frames → optional stop command ($F2) → ready signal ($F0) → handshake poll → start command ($FF) → wait → SpcBlockTransfer for bulk data → play command. The transfer runs only when the script's group byte ($06F4, stored at the top of the routine) equals musicRoomGroup; otherwise the routine returns. The redundancy check is CheckSourceCacheHit on $0687, which skips a load of the same source.

=== SCRIPT POINTER ADDRESS MAPPING ===

LoadScriptPointer reads 3-byte ROM pointers from the script stream and applies SNES address space mapping: bank bytes $00-$6F are offset to $80-$EF (LoROM → HiROM equivalent), banks $70-$9F use an additional $20 offset with bit 15 clearing on the address word. This translates script-embedded compact pointers to the full 24-bit addresses needed for DMA and indirect access.
shadow_shimmer:
Shadow's palette shimmer (Bank 02, 176654-176798): a hidden companion that animates the player's OBJ palette 0 (colours $81-$8F) while the player is Shadow (characterForm 2).

SPAWN: PlayerCharacterDef (SpawnListAppend, so it is appended at the end of the actor list) and the two Dark Space transformations in sE6_gaia (Transform_WillToShadow, Transform_FreedanToShadow), which spawn it just before they set characterForm = 2; the new actor runs later in the same tick, after the form is set. All three use flags $2800: hidden ($2000) plus $0800, so it also runs in the cutscene-only passes. Init dies at once when characterForm is not 2.

STRUCTURE: Init spawns ShadowShimmerSlowStrips with SpawnAfterMarked (a marked child dies with its parent). This actor never touches the palette: it only points the child at one of three routines by writing the child's entry word ($0000,Y) and clearing its waitCounter ($0008,Y). The child is found through $06 (the actor-list successor), which is the child because SpawnAfter inserts it directly behind its spawner.
  - ShadowShimmerSlowStrips: bundle #23 in a loop (eight strips, wait 2 each)
  - ShadowShimmerFastStrips: bundle #24 in a loop (eight strips, waits 0 and 1 alternating: a faster cycle)
  - ShadowShimmerNop: yields every frame, no palette change
Both bundles write colours $81-$8F (15 colours, size byte $1D); bundle #23 is also the Shadow palette that global_ambient_dispatcher loads at spawn.

STATES: Idle (the slow strips, ShadowShimmerSlowStrips) and Active (the fast strips, ShadowShimmerFastStrips). Idle -> Active when playerSpeedEw or playerSpeedNs is nonzero, or when flag byte #00 is set. Active -> Idle when both speeds are zero and flag #00 is clear. The speed words are not set by ordinary walking (walking uses the joypad velocity of player_move_controller); they are nonzero during slope and ramp slides and in run / slide moves, so the fast strips play then. Flag #00 is a general per-scene flag (scene_lifecycle clears it at scene setup; scene_flag_init sets it in 26 scene lists; some scripts set and clear it) that player_character also reads to pick Shadow's idle, ladder and shimmy-detach sprites; where it is set, this actor stays in Active. What the flag means is not traced.

GUARD (ShadowShimmerGuard, called every frame from both states): characterForm no longer 2 -> pop the return address and Die (the marked child dies too). Player Flags10 bit $0040 (dead: set when HP reaches 0 by combat_collision and by GameOverSequence; combat_collision also calls it the orb state) -> point the child at ShadowShimmerNop and run SetEntryHere + RTL. The saved entry is that RTL, so the states are never run again for the rest of the scene visit and the palette stays on whatever strip was showing.
ShowDialogueFrame:
Bank-1 dialogue rendering wrapper — sets data bank and renders one dialogue frame (192584–192618, Bank 02).

A thin wrapper that bridges the bank-2 game engine to the DialogStringRenderer in bank 1 ($81 in HiROM). The dialogue system keeps its string data and rendering tables in bank $01/$81, so the data bank register (DBR) must be set to $81 before calling DialogStringRenderer for DB-relative data access to work correctly.

Input: Y = dialogue string pointer, passed through to DialogStringRenderer (UpdateFrameRender saves and restores Y).

=== SEQUENCE ===

1. Save processor flags and data bank (PHP, PHB)
2. Save joypadMaskStd and zero it — unmasks all buttons during dialogue rendering so the dialogue system can check for button presses without interference from the game's input mask
3. Set DBR = $81 (PHA #$81, PLB) — dialogue data lives in bank $01/$81
4. UpdateFrameRender — render-only frame update (sprite composition, palette/display processing, HDMA, HUD, VBlank sync; no actor AI) before processing dialogue
5. DialogStringRenderer — the actual bank-1 dialogue engine that processes dialogue string commands, renders text glyphs, handles dialogue box open/close, and manages text scrolling
6. Restore joypadMaskStd, data bank, and processor flags

Callers: treasure-chest handling (warps_interaction) and item-giving NPC interaction (combat_collision InteractionDamage_NPCChat), which show item-get / inventory-full strings.
slope_ramp_physics:
Slope/ramp terrain physics and flat-ground deceleration - SpawnAfter companion of the player actor (177195-178099, Bank 02).

PlayerCharacterDef spawns it with SpawnAfter, so it sits right behind the player actor in the actor list and runs every frame after the player's own scripts. It never moves the player. It only edits playerSpeedEw / playerSpeedNs (and the playerFlags $1000 latch); player_move_controller turns those speeds into movement (speed x 4 plus external velocity) in the same frame: the actor list order is attack, player, slope, controller, so the controller runs right after this actor.

=== FRAME FLOW (SlopePhysicsEntry) ===

1. Gate: if the player actor's $10 has bit $0080 or bit $0040 set (hit marker / orb state) and iframeCounter is not negative, slope detection is skipped and only SlopeFlatDecelerate runs.
2. Speed nonzero (EW or NS): probe the collision tile at (actor X, actor Y - 8) with TileProbeMain, look the type up in SlopeTileDispatch and jump to the handler. A type with no handler goes to the transition-tile test (below), otherwise to SlopeFlatExit.
3. Speed zero and playerFlags $1000 set: reset both step counters and probe four cells (below). A slope found runs its handler, none goes to SlopeFlatExit.
4. Speed zero and no latch: SlopeFlatDecelerate.
A slope handler adds one curve value to one axis (ApplySlopeCurve*) and returns through ClampSpeeds.

=== TILE TYPES (SlopeTileDispatch) ===

| Type | Handler | Pushes the player | Curve |
|------|---------|-------------------|-------|
| $03  | SlopeType03Handler | south (NS +) | slopeCurvePtrB |
| $05  | SlopeType05Handler | west (EW -) | slopeCurvePtrA, negated |
| $0A  | SlopeType0AHandler | east (EW +) | slopeCurvePtrA |
| $0C  | SlopeType0CHandler | north (NS -) | slopeCurvePtrB, negated |

All other types (0-2, 4, 6-9, B, D-F) have a zero entry: no slope. The table holds the handler addresses; the dispatch does DEC, PHA, RTS so that the RTS lands on the handler. Whether a handler pushes DOWNHILL was not checked against the map art; the direction column is what the code does to the speed.

=== CURVES ===

slopeCurvePtrA ($09BA, east-west) and slopeCurvePtrB ($09BC, north-south) both point at the start of the math_lookup_tables block, and decelCurvePtr ($09C2) at that block + $20; system_core sets them once at boot. Each curve is 16 words, read as (counter & $0F) x 2 bytes from the pointer. Default slope curve: $0001 at steps 0, 4, 8 and 12, otherwise 0, i.e. +1 speed unit every fourth frame. Default deceleration curve: $0001 at steps 7 and 15. slopeStepCounter ($09B6) advances once per frame on a slope and is cleared when the slope speed reaches zero, when SlopeFlatExit runs and on every frame of the stopped probe (so a slope always starts at step 0). decelStepCounter ($09B8) advances on EVERY ReadDecelerationStep call, including calls that return 0. maxSpeedEw / maxSpeedNs ($09C8 / $09CA) are set to 9 in system_core and not written again in the extracted code; ClampSpeeds limits |speed| to max - 1 = 8.

=== THE $1000 ON-SLOPE LATCH (playerFlags) ===

Set by the ramp walkers (player_move_ramps, player_move_west) while the player traverses a ramp and by these handlers when a slope curve brings an axis speed to exactly zero. Cleared by player_move_controller whenever the EW or the NS speed is nonzero, and by SlopeFlatDecelerate when EW speed is zero. While it is set player_move_controller drops the joypad velocity, DecelerateEW / DecelerateNS return at once, the Aura Barrier cannot be used and the walk code skips its L/R block check. By this reading a player at rest on the latch gets no joypad movement: the four-cell probe finds the slope again, the first curve step (+1 or -1) gives a nonzero speed, and the next controller pass clears the latch.

=== TRANSITION TILES $06 AND $09 ===

If the tile under the probe has no handler but is type $06 or $09, the code looks at two other cells with MapCellDown (one map row below the probe tile) and then MapCellUp (one row above), both relative to the index TileProbeMain left in $00. A type $05 or $0A in either cell runs that handler; otherwise SlopeFlatExit. The earlier text said "right and left adjacent cells"; MapCellDown/Up step by rows (+/-$10), MapCellRight/Left by columns.

=== STOPPED-ON-SLOPE PROBE ===

Four cells are tested in this order: the probe cell, the cell to its RIGHT (MapCellRight), the cell BELOW it (MapCellDown) and the cell below-right (MapCellRight from the new base; the code stores the new index in $00 after MapCellDown). The first slope type found runs its handler. The probe point here is playerXPos / playerYPos (camera_scroll_controller writes actor X - 8 and actor Y - $10 there), while the moving probe uses (actor X, actor Y - 8); the two phases therefore look at different points (open question).

=== DECELERATION (SlopeFlatDecelerate, DecelerateEW / DecelerateNS) ===

SlopeFlatDecelerate decelerates the EW axis when EW speed is nonzero and then returns; the NS axis is only handled on a frame in which EW speed is already zero (after clearing the $1000 latch). Per axis: skipped while the latch is set; |speed| < 3 is set to zero at once (the step counter is not reset); otherwise a D-pad bit for the direction of travel suppresses deceleration, else one curve value is subtracted (added for negative speeds) and, whether that step was applied or returned 0, a D-pad bit for the opposite direction applies a second curve value (braking). Reaching zero resets decelStepCounter in the EW routine; the NS routine resets slopeStepCounter instead (probable copy slip, open question).

=== OTHER QUIRKS (open questions) ===

ClampSpeeds examines the NS speed only when EW speed is zero. ReadDecelerationStepNS is a byte-for-byte copy of ReadDecelerationStep (same counter, same curve). slopeFracAccum ($09C6) is the sub-pixel accumulator of the north/south slope walkers (player_move_south, player_move_ns); this file only clears it (SlopeFlatExit), as player_move_controller does when the NS speed is zero.
spc_transfer:
SPC700 audio processor data transfer system (168078–171490, Bank 02).

Implements the SNES-to-SPC700 upload protocol used to load the game's sound engine at boot and every music track afterwards into the SPC700's 64 KB RAM (ARAM). All communication goes through the four I/O ports APUIO0–APUIO3 ($2140–$2143): a CPU read returns what the SPC wrote to its port, a CPU write goes to the SPC's input port.

=== IPL PROTOCOL (SpcIplHandshake) ===
The SPC700 boot ROM (IPL) and the sound engine's resident clone of it (sub_0f89, entered by port command $FF; docs/audio/spc-disassembly.md) speak the same byte-stream protocol, so one 65816 routine serves both:
1. The SPC posts $BBAA on ports 0/1 when it is ready.
2. A record is size (word), ARAM destination (word) and size data bytes. The CPU writes the destination to ports 2/3, port 1 = 1 (data follows) or 0 (size 0: end of session), then a kick value on port 0 ($CC for the first record) and waits for the SPC to echo it.
3. Each data byte is one 16-bit write to ports 0/1 (counter in the low byte, data in the high byte; the counter starts at 0 and increments per byte). The CPU waits for the SPC to echo the counter before sending the next byte.
4. After the last byte the code waits for the final echo; the carry from that equal compare makes ADC #$03 add 4, and a result of 0 is stepped over, so the next record's kick is non-zero and differs from the last counter.
5. A record of size 0 ends the session. For the boot ROM its destination word is the entry address the SPC jumps to; the resident loader just returns to the engine.
The V flag carries 'more records follow': ROL puts the size-nonzero carry into port 1 (0 or 1) and ADC #$7F overflows only when it was 1.

=== NMI STATE ===
Both transfer routines call DisableNmiKeepJoypad (NMITIMEN = $01: NMI OFF, joypad auto-read on) just before each header and kick, so the NMI cannot interleave with the port writes. After the SPC echoes the kick they call EnableNmiAndJoypad only if worldReadyFlag = $0F, so once the game is running the data bytes are sent with NMI enabled (the NMI then runs UpdateFrameFull; the music change in the main loop relies on it); at boot the NMI stays off.

=== ROUTINES ===
SpcLoadBuiltinEngine (boot, from SystemInit): [$46] = spc_sound_engine, then SpcIplHandshake. The blob is one record (size $0BCA = 3,018 bytes of SPC700 code and tables to ARAM $0400) followed by the terminator record (size 0, entry $0400): 168464–171490.
SpcIplHandshake: sends the records at [$46] from Y = 0 until the size-0 record, leaving Y just past it.
SpcBlockTransfer (music; callers: LoadMusicFromTransitionState and scene_script's music load): two sessions on one stream. Session 1 = SpcIplHandshake over the stream's leading records (the song data and tables, e.g. ARAM $1254, $1300, $5532, $1038, $0FFC, $0FFE, $0FE0; the words at ARAM $0FFC/$0FFE are the engine's stream and tail pointers). The stream continues after the terminator: its destination word is reused as the ARAM address of the first sample chunk, then one count byte and that many chunk-index bytes. Port command $FF re-enters the engine's loader (a fresh $BBAA, awaited at 168114) and session 2 sends the chunks from the sample library at $C5:0000: chunk = [size word][data], stored back to back (61 chunks, indices 0-60), in 32 KB pages (the pointer $4A wraps at $8000 into the next bank, even inside a chunk). For each index byte the code walks the library from the start to that chunk (skipping chunks by their size words), sends it to the running ARAM address (previous chunk's destination + size) and moves on; an index with bit 7 set is an empty slot and is skipped. A final size-0 record ends session 2.

The library, the index lists and the records are data; the SPC engine's own behavior is documented in docs/audio/.
system_init:
Boot-time hardware and RAM initialisation plus two per-frame VBlank DMA routines (Bank 02).

- InitHardwareRegisters and InitSystemVariables are boot code: SystemInit (system_core) calls them once, in that order, with DBR = $81 (so the absolute $0000,Y stores below reach the LowRAM mirror and the $2100/$4200 registers).
- UploadCgramPalette and UploadOamTable are NOT boot code: the NMI handler calls them every VBlank (steps 5 and 6 of NmiHandler); UploadCgramPalette is also called by the camera refresh (camera_tilemap) and by the inventory overlay. They assume the NMI register state: A already 8-bit, index registers 16-bit (they contain no REP/SEP for X).
- DmaFixedByteFill is the zero-fill helper of InitSystemVariables.

=== WRAM clear ===
Three fixed-source DMA passes through the WRAM port ($2180): $0000-$00FF ($100 bytes), then from $0200 for $FF00 bytes (7E:0200 up to 7F:00FF; the WRAM address is 17 bits wide and keeps counting across the bank boundary), then the next $FF00 bytes without resetting the address (7F:0100-7F:FFFF). Total $1FF00 bytes: all 128 KB except the stack page $0100-$01FF. The zero byte is read from the ROM (first byte of math_lookup_tables.sine_table_8bit, sin(0) = $00).

=== SystemInitConstants (34 word writes, ;00-;21) ===
Layer map bases mapTilemapBaseA/B = $A000/$C000; DP $80-$82 = the collision map long pointer $7F:C000 (see AGENTS: never corrupt it); bgTilemapVramBase = $1000/$1800 (matches BG1SC/BG2SC below); metatileDefBase = $2000 (layer 0) and $06B0 = $2800 (layer 1, unnamed second word of the same array); strip staging pointers; collisionFlagTableL0/L1 = $0000/$0100 (offsets inside bank $7F); scene_meta pointer in $3A/$3C; the RAM stub bytes $0402 = 8B 54 and $0406 = AB 60 (PHB; MVN; PLB; RTS with the two MVN bank bytes filled in at $0404/$0405 when used); $5E/$60/$62 = 0/$0081/0 (consumers not traced); gfxCacheIdxB = 1, gfxCacheIdxA = $0404 (also the address of the stub's MVN operand pair); the joypad remap words remapL $0020, remapR $0010, remapB $4008, remapA $8080, remapY $0040, remapX $0004, remapSelect $2000, remapStart $1000 (db-us/transforms.json rewrites the four face-button defaults from the vanilla ROM values); $0B14 = $003C (no reader found anywhere in extracted); inventoryEquippedIndex = $FFFF; $0B04 = 0 (saved dialog frame delay that DialogStringRenderer restores).

=== PpuRegisterInitTable (76 writes, ;00-;4B) ===
Disables DMA/HDMA, INIDISP $80 (forced blank), OBJSEL $02, BGMODE $09 (mode 1 with BG3 on top), BG1SC $11 / BG2SC $19 (VRAM $1000 / $1800, 64x32), BG3SC $78, BG12NBA $22, BG34NBA $06 (BG3 characters at $6000: the dialog font), zeroed scroll/Mode 7 registers (the two writes per register fill both bytes of the write-twice ports; M7A = $0100), VMAIN $80, window masks $33 with WH1 $FF, TM $04 (only BG3 on the main screen), CGWSEL $82, COLDATA $E0, NMITIMEN 0, WRIO $FF, and MEMSEL 0 as the LAST entry. SystemInit stores MEMSEL = 1 before calling InitHardwareRegisters, so this entry switches FastROM timing back off; sFB_boot_logo turns it on again later. Data ports and CGADD data ($2104, $2118/9, $2122) are not part of the table.
tile_collision:
Tile collision primitives: corner probes, collision-byte reader, map-cell stepping and movement helpers for the player (188674–189334, Bank 02). Outputs to system/player/ next to its callers.

Callers: every player_move_* block (main, ns, south, east, diag, ramps), the slope_ramp_physics actor (actors/player) and map_coords (FindSlopeForWestMove / FindSlopeForEastMove, which borrow the probes and MapCell steps). Nothing outside the player/slope code uses them (the earlier note said only the player_move_* blocks do).

=== COLLISION BYTE ===

The collision layer ($7FC000, one byte per 16x16 tile) holds the terrain type in the low nibble and, in the high nibble, the solid mark that actors OR in with MarkSolidHere / MarkSolidOffset / MarkSolidAbs ($F0) and remove with the Clear ops. ReadCollisionNibble returns the high nibble shifted down when it is nonzero ($F0 becomes $0F, solid) and the terrain type otherwise. Types seen by callers: $05 west-facing slope, $0A east-facing slope, $07 ladder, $06 and $09 wall-like types (meaning not decoded; see tile_collision_physics), $0E and above solid.

=== CORNER PROBES ===

Eight probes sample the corners of the 16x16 hitbox, whose reference point is the centre of the bottom edge: left = pixel - 8, right = pixel + 7, top = pixel - 16, bottom = pixel - 1 (ProbeCurrentTL/TR/BL/BR use $22/$26, ProbeFutureTL/TR/BL/BR use $22 + $20 and $26 + $24; sub-pixels are shifted down by 2 first). Each stores the probe pixel in $1A (X) and $1E (Y) and calls TileProbeMain. Return protocol: A = collision type; carry set when the type is NONZERO, which includes slopes, ladders and wall types as well as solid tiles (callers compare A with $0E for solid); carry clear for type 0. Out of bounds gives A = $0F, carry set.

The INC $1A / INC $1E after the call in the TR, BL and BR probes move the stored right or bottom coordinate one pixel past the hitbox edge (+8, bottom + 1). That is what makes CheckSubTileAlignX/Y ($1A / $1E & $0F = 0) test 'is this edge flush with a tile boundary' for all four edges (TL needs no INC: its left and top edges are already the first covered pixel). It is not a shift 'inward for MapCell navigation': the MapCell steps start from the map index in $00.

=== TILE PROBE ENGINE ===

TileProbeMain checks $1A and $1E against the camera bounds (cameraOffsetX/Y up to cameraBoundsX / cameraLowerYBound; negative values are rejected too). Out of bounds: $00 = $4001, A = $0F, carry set. In bounds: tile column $18 = $1A >> 4, tile row $1C = $1E >> 4, CalcTileMapOffset (tile_collision_physics) returns the map index in Y, which is stored in $00 and passed in X to ReadCollisionNibble.

=== MAP CELL STEPS ===

The map index is page (high byte) and row/column nibbles (low byte): +$10 in the low byte is one row down, +1 one column right. MapCellDown / MapCellUp add or subtract $10 and, on carry or borrow, add or subtract mapRowStrideL0 in the high byte; MapCellRight / MapCellLeft step the low byte and, when the column nibble wraps, step the high byte (one page right or left) and undo the row step with + or - $F0, which lands on column 0 of the next page (right) or column 15 of the previous page (left), same row. Each returns the new index in X; none reads or writes $1A/$1E. Equivalent to the map_coords MapIndexMove* routines. Some callers (slope_ramp_physics) still describe MapCellDown as the 'right' cell.

=== MOVEMENT HELPERS ===

ApplyMovementDeltas: $22 += $20, $26 += $24, then both velocities are zeroed (standard epilogue of an unblocked step). ClearMovementDeltas zeroes $20 and $24. SetActorCollisionFlag ORs $0004 into the flags word at actor + $10 (solid contact this tick) for the actor slot in $000A. CheckTileBoundaryXor tests whether the X step crosses a 16-pixel column. CombinedProbe_Unused has no call site.
vblank_joypad:
VBlank synchronization, Mode 7 register upload, and joypad processing with button remapping (163899–164305, Bank 02).

Two entry points share the Mode 7 and joypad pipeline:
- VBlankPartial: skips the NMI wait; its only caller is UpdateFrameFull (system_core), which runs inside the NMI handler
- VBlankWaitAndJoypad: polls RDNMI until VBlank begins, then falls through

=== NMI COOPERATION ===
The hardware joypad value is NOT read here. The NMI handler (step 11) waits for the auto-read to finish and stores JOY1L in joypadRaw; this routine then replaces joypadRaw with the REMAPPED value. It therefore only sees fresh hardware data when the NMI has run since the previous call (NMI enabled while waiting, or called from inside the NMI as VBlankPartial). Called with NMI disabled it would remap an already remapped joypadRaw again, which is not idempotent for swapped or software-only mappings.

=== MODE 7 UPLOAD ===
When scrollModeFlags bit 3 is set, uploads the Mode 7 affine transformation matrix (M7A–M7D) and rotation center (M7X, M7Y) from WRAM shadow registers ($C2–$CD) to PPU write-twice registers ($211B–$2120). Each register requires two consecutive 8-bit writes (low byte, then high byte). Center point high bytes are masked to 5 bits (AND #$1F) for the 13-bit signed coordinate range. Also snapshots BG scroll positions ($BE/$C0 → $CE/$D0) with LDX/STX: X is not saved by this routine, so X is clobbered in Mode 7 scenes (A and P are preserved).

=== JOYPAD INJECT ===
If joypadInject ($09AC) is nonzero, the value becomes joypadCurrent, joypadInject is cleared and the routine returns at once. The injection is one-shot (a script must rewrite it every frame to hold buttons, as sc06_bill does; sg4C_auto_advance writes $FFFF once) and it bypasses everything below: no remapping, no consumption mask, no auto-repeat and no joypadMaskStd, and joypadRaw is left as the hardware value. Writers in extracted/: sg4C_auto_advance, sc06_bill; scene_lifecycle clears it on scene change.

=== BUTTON REMAPPING ===
The D-pad (bits 8–11, $0F00) always passes through directly. Then each physical button is checked against its remap entry: if the button is pressed in joypadRaw and the remap value is nonzero, the remap value (an arbitrary 16-bit logical mask) is TSB'd into joypadRemapped. A button whose remap value is zero never appears. The remap values live in $0DA6–$0DB4 (the diary menu edits them); db-us/transforms.json rewrites some of their defaults. The low nibble of a hardware read is always 0 ($0008/$0004 are not hardware buttons), so a remap target may use those bits as software-only logical buttons.

Remap variable → physical button checked (the names refer to the physical button):
  remapStart→Start($1000)  remapSelect→Select($2000)  remapB→B($8000)  remapY→Y($4000)
  remapA→A($0080)  remapX→X($0040)  remapL→L($0020)  remapR→R($0010)

SNES joypad bit layout (16-bit auto-read from $4218/$4219):
  $8000=B  $4000=Y  $2000=Sel  $1000=Start  $0800=Up  $0400=Dn
  $0200=Left  $0100=Right  $0080=A  $0040=X  $0020=L  $0010=R

=== CONSUMPTION MASK + EDGE DETECTION ===
joypadHeld serves as a cooperative consumption mask. Game code marks buttons as consumed via TSB $joypadHeld when processing input events. This routine then:
1. Copies remapped → joypadCurrent and joypadRaw
2. ANDs joypadHeld with the remapped buttons — retains only consumed buttons still physically pressed
3. Applies the auto-repeat rule below (which may drop repeat-eligible bits from joypadHeld)
4. TRBs joypadHeld from joypadCurrent — removes consumed buttons — and then joypadMaskStd
Result: joypadCurrent = newly pressed buttons + auto-repeat triggers. A consumed button does not reappear until it is released and pressed again (or auto-repeat fires).

=== AUTO-REPEAT ===
Buttons in joypadMaskInv (the repeat mask; the dialog handler and the diary menu set it to $0F00, the D-pad) that are consumed and still held are repeat-eligible:
- joypadRepeatCounter increments on each call while at least one is held
- on the 12th call the eligible bits are cleared from joypadHeld BEFORE it is subtracted from joypadCurrent, so the repeat shows up in joypadCurrent in the same call; the counter is reset, so the first repeat comes 12 calls after the press was consumed and the following ones every 12 calls while the game code keeps consuming them
- the counter is also reset whenever no consumed button in the mask is held

joypadMaskStd is TRB'd from joypadCurrent at the end to unconditionally suppress certain buttons (never from the injected value).

=== UTILITY ROUTINES ===
EnableNmiAndJoypad: $81 → NMITIMEN (NMI + joypad auto-read).
DisableNmiKeepJoypad: $01 → NMITIMEN: turns the NMI OFF and leaves only joypad auto-read on.
ScreenBlackout: $00 → INIDISP (forced blank OFF, brightness 0 — screen appears black but PPU remains active; does NOT set the SNES forced blank bit).
EnterForcedBlank: $80 → INIDISP (forced blank ON — PPU halted, VRAM/OAM/CGRAM accessible for DMA transfers).
WaitFrames: loop VBlankWaitAndJoypad for A frames (A = 0 would wait 256 frames, or 65,536 with a 16-bit A).
vram_buffer_clear:
BG3 tilemap buffer clear — zeroes the BG3 tilemap staging buffer at $7F:0200 (192618–192652, Bank 02).

The buffer is a 32×32-word BG3 tilemap (2048 bytes, 64 bytes per tilemap row). The HUD, dialogue, console-text, menu and radar renderers write tilemap words into it; when displayModeFlags bit 0 is set the engine DMAs it to VRAM $7800 (BG3SC = $78).

Two entry points:

- ClearBg3TilemapBuffer_PreserveHud: Zeroes offsets $0140–$07FF. The first $0140 bytes (160 words = 5 tilemap rows) are kept — that is exactly the span LoadHudTilemap fills (HudTilemapData expands to 159 words), so the HUD survives overlay teardown (inferred from the stream length).
- ClearBg3TilemapBuffer_Full: Zeroes the whole buffer, offsets $0000–$07FF.

Both share one word-write loop. Clobbers A; preserves X and P. Assembled for 16-bit index registers (it does not REP #$10 itself).
warps_interaction:
Warp system, treasure chest interaction, and opened-chest redraw (173533–174986, Bank 02).

Combines three related subsystems: scene-transition warps, treasure chest opening, and redrawing already-opened chests when a scene is built (PlaceOpenedChestTiles). The chest code reads per-scene records from scene_chest_table, the warp code reads warp rectangles from scene_warps. CheckWarpAndChest is called every frame from the main loop (system_core); InitWarpTable and PlaceOpenedChestTiles run while a scene is set up (scene_lifecycle; PlaceOpenedChestTiles again when inventory_overlay rebuilds the scene).

=== WARP SYSTEM ===

InitWarpTable sets up two warp table pointers for the current scene:
- $00D4: Standard warp entries (12 bytes each) — scene-transition warps
- $00D6: Extended warp entries (13 bytes each) — in-scene forced-walk warps

The two tables are stored contiguously in scene_warps, separated by an $FF terminator byte. InitWarpTable walks past the standard entries to find the extended table start.

CheckWarpRectangles tests the player's tile and pixel position against both tables:
1. Standard warps: tile-level AABB check (playerXTile/playerYTile vs entry bytes 0-3), then sub-tile pixel refinement via ConvertWarpToPixels. Hit → ExecuteWarp.
2. Extended warps: same AABB structure but 13-byte entries (bytes 4–5 camera window, byte 6 direction/sequence, bytes 7–12 walk steps). Hit → ExecuteForcedWalkWarp for forced-walk warp.

ConvertWarpToPixels converts tile coordinates to pixel coordinates (×16) and computes the bounding box size (width/height × 16 − 15) for sub-tile precision checking.

ExecuteWarp copies the standard entry into the transition parameters: destination scene ($0642, byte 4), player spawn X/Y ($064C/$064E, bytes 5–8), facing ($0650, byte 9 with bit 7 masked off) and the packed camera window read by InitCameraBounds ($0652, bytes 10–11). It also records the source scene ($0B12), the source rectangle bytes 0–3 ($0B08/$0B0C/$0B0A/$0B0E) and two camera bytes ($0B10/$0B11) holding bits 8–11 of the camera offset X/Y and of the camera bounds X/Y. Every warp stores a pointer to entry+4 and the scene_warps bank in $0AF4/$0AF6: GameOverSequence reloads from it when the player dies with 100 or more gems (revive). If bit 7 of entry byte 9 is set the same pointer is also stored in sceneSaveData ($0AF0/$0AF2), which GameOverSequence uses for a real game over (fewer than 100 gems). Both variants return carry set.

ExecuteForcedWalkWarp handles extended (forced-walk) warps: checks the $0100 re-entry guard in playerFlags, stores the camera window, direction/sequence byte and walk-step pointer, calls InitCameraBounds, and spawns a direction-specific forced walk actor via StartForcedWalk.

StartForcedWalk decodes the direction from scrollStepTableBase: bit 5 = West, bit 4 = East, bit 7 = North, default = South. Spawns the corresponding ForcedWalk actor (ForcedWalkSouth/West/East/North) as a SpawnBefore on the player actor. Sets playerFlags $0100 (forced walk active) and bit 13 ($2000, script-driven tick) in the player actor's flags word $10.

=== CHEST INTERACTION SYSTEM ===

HandleChestInteraction runs every frame (via CheckWarpAndChest) and opens a chest when the player pushes against it from below. All of these must hold, otherwise it returns at once:
1. layerPriorityFlag bit $0200 clear (field interaction not disabled)
2. Player actor flag $10 bit 2 ($0004) set: the solid-contact flag of the collision code, i.e. the player is touching a solid tile
3. joypadCurrent bit $0800 (D-pad up) set
4. GetPlayerFacingDirection == 1 (north; the same code order as the facing COP operands)

The chest tile search reads mapLayerTilemap at the tile in front of the player. Tile $F8 = chest bottom-left, $F9 = chest bottom-right (the 2×2 closed chest uses base $F8: bottom $F8/$F9, top $FA/$FB). If the tile is $F9 the left neighbour must be $F8, and the origin X is decremented, so the origin is always the bottom-left cell.

The routine then walks the scene's records in scene_chest_table (scene index $0646) comparing byte 0/1 (X, Y of the bottom-left cell) with the origin. No match: the chest is shown the message dialog_chest_locked ("The jewel box is tightly closed.").

A matching record is processed according to its byte 2 (contents):
- Nonzero: item chest. displayModeFlags bit 7 is set (display-filter mode: only actors flagged $1000 keep running), the open chest tiles (base $FC) are drawn, then GiveItemToPlayer runs. Success without record byte 3 bit 7: clear the display filter, SFX #$2A, ShowDialogueFrame with dialog_item_chest (prints the item name held in $0DB8), SetEventFlag. Success with byte 3 bit 7: spawn ChestOpeningActor (fanfare with music transition) and SetEventFlag. Inventory full: show the dialogue string GiveItemToPlayer returned in Y (dialog_item_full, "Your inventory's full!"), redraw the closed tiles (base $F8) and do not set the flag.
- Zero: flag-only chest: dialog_chest_empty ("It is empty!"), then SetEventFlag.
In both cases the event flag is record byte 3 AND $7F.

DrawChestTiles places a 2×2 chest at the record's position, queuing each tile to QueueVisibleTileVram for an immediate VRAM update. Tile IDs: base+2, base+3 (top row, Y−1), base, base+1 (bottom row), where base is $FC for an open chest and $F8 for a closed one.

=== CHEST OPENING ACTOR ===

ChestOpeningActor runs the fanfare for chests whose record has byte 3 bit 7 set. The music value it handles is the one in musicParentActor ($06F2); other code calls that word the original music ID, so the name is a misnomer. The sequence:
1. Saves $06F2 in orbitAngle (per-actor scratch) and spawns SpcTransferMusicData (async SPC upload) as a child; the pool-full result ($1FC0) jumps to the cleanup.
2. Gives the child its track number (the $26 field set by HandleChestInteraction, #$17, plus 1) in chatPtr and flags it $1000 so it still runs while the world is frozen.
3. Masks the joypad ($CFFC into joypadMaskStd: every button except Select/Start), flags the player $1000, points the player's state at PlayerIdleAnimLoop and sets playerFlags $0800 (script lock).
4. Yields until musicTransitionState == $FFFF (upload finished), then spawns ChestDialogueActor with the dialogue pointer ($24) and the item ID ($20).
5. Yields until APUIO1 reads $FF, then releases the player (RestorePlayerControlDirect, clears the $1000 flag) and unmasks the joypad.
6. Spawns a second SpcTransferMusicData whose track value is the saved $06F2 (restoring the scene music), waits for $FFFF again, WaitByte #0B (12 ticks), clears displayModeFlags bit 7 and dies.

ChestDialogueActor: WaitByte #48 (73 ticks), clears its own $1000 flag, restores the item ID from $20 to $0DB8 (the dialogue string prints the item name from there), shows the dialogue pointer stored in $24 with ShowDialogueFrame, and dies.

=== OPENED-CHEST REDRAW (PlaceOpenedChestTiles) ===

PlaceOpenedChestTiles walks the scene's records in scene_chest_table. For each record whose event flag (byte 3 AND $7F, TestEventFlag_0200) is set, it writes the OPEN-chest 2×2 pattern at the record position:
  Top-left: $FE, Top-right: $FF (row Y−1)
  Bottom-left: $FC, Bottom-right: $FD (row Y)
These are exactly the tiles DrawChestTiles draws with base $FC, and the records are the chest records, so the routine restores chests the player has already opened whenever the scene map is rebuilt (scene load, and inventory_overlay's scene reload). The earlier "closed door/barrier" reading is not supported by the code. Only the map is written; no VRAM update is queued.

=== UTILITY ===

SetAnimStatePointer: Sets a function pointer ($0000,Y) and clears the frame counter ($0008,Y) for an actor. Used by ChestOpeningActor to override the player's animation state during the chest opening sequence.
